typedef hwloc_const_bitmap_t hwloc_const_cpuset_t;
objects.description: Alias types for CPU sets represented by hwloc bitmaps. They indicate processor affinity masks. These are typedefs to hwloc_bitmap_t or const variant; all bitmap APIs apply.

objects.definition:

typedef hwloc_const_bitmap_t hwloc_const_nodeset_t;
objects.description: Alias types for NUMA node sets represented by hwloc bitmaps. Used to specify/track memory node affinity. Typedefs to hwloc_bitmap_t or const variant.

objects.definition:
typedef enum {
#define HWLOC_OBJ_TYPE_MIN HWLOC_OBJ_MACHINE
  HWLOC_OBJ_MACHINE,
  HWLOC_OBJ_PACKAGE,
  HWLOC_OBJ_DIE,
  HWLOC_OBJ_CORE,
  HWLOC_OBJ_PU,
  HWLOC_OBJ_L1CACHE,
  HWLOC_OBJ_L2CACHE,
  HWLOC_OBJ_L3CACHE,
  HWLOC_OBJ_L4CACHE,
  HWLOC_OBJ_L5CACHE,
  HWLOC_OBJ_L1ICACHE,
  HWLOC_OBJ_L2ICACHE,
  HWLOC_OBJ_L3ICACHE,
  HWLOC_OBJ_GROUP,
  HWLOC_OBJ_NUMANODE,
  HWLOC_OBJ_MEMCACHE,
  HWLOC_OBJ_BRIDGE,
  HWLOC_OBJ_PCI_DEVICE,
  HWLOC_OBJ_OS_DEVICE,
  HWLOC_OBJ_MISC,
  HWLOC_OBJ_TYPE_MAX
} hwloc_obj_type_t;
objects.description: Enumeration of object types used in the topology (Machine, Package, Core, PU, caches, NUMA nodes, I/O, Misc, etc.). Ordering should not be relied upon; use hwloc_compare_types().
Enumeration of cache kinds (unified, data, instruction) for cache attributes.
Enumeration of bridge side types for I/O bridges (host side vs PCI side).
Bitmask type indicating one or more OS device categories (storage, memory device, GPU, co-processor, network, OpenFabrics, DMA).
Name/value string pair used as an info attribute attached to objects and to the topology.
Container for an array of info string pairs used on objects and topologies. Modify via hwloc_obj_add_info() or hwloc_modify_infos().

Core structure representing a topology object (Normal, Memory, I/O, Misc). Contains hierarchy links, children lists, cpusets/nodesets, attributes, infos, and user data. Do not modify fields except userdata; sets should be duplicated before modification.
Type-specific attribute container for an hwloc_obj. Holds NUMA, cache, group, PCI device, bridge, or OS device attributes depending on object type.

objects.definition: struct hwloc_topology; typedef struct hwloc_topology * hwloc_topology_t;
objects.description: Opaque handle for a topology context. Allocate with hwloc_topology_init() and build with hwloc_topology_load(); free with hwloc_topology_destroy().
Negative virtual depths and special return codes used with depth queries for non-normal object classes or ambiguous cases.
Flags that control verbosity and formatting when stringifying object types and attributes.
Operations for modifying arrays of info attributes (add, add-unique, replace, remove).
Bitmask flags refining CPU binding operations (bind process vs thread, strictness, avoid implicit membind).
Enumeration of memory binding policies (default, first-touch, bind, interleave, weighted interleave, next-touch, mixed).
Bitmask flags refining memory binding operations (scope, strictness, migration, avoid CPU bind effects, set kind).
Flags for component selection; currently only allows blacklisting components or phases.

objects.definition:
enum hwloc_topology_flags_e {
  HWLOC_TOPOLOGY_FLAG_INCLUDE_DISALLOWED = (1UL<<0),
  HWLOC_TOPOLOGY_FLAG_IS_THISSYSTEM = (1UL<<1),
  HWLOC_TOPOLOGY_FLAG_THISSYSTEM_ALLOWED_RESOURCES = (1UL<<2),
  HWLOC_TOPOLOGY_FLAG_IMPORT_SUPPORT = (1UL<<3),
  HWLOC_TOPOLOGY_FLAG_RESTRICT_TO_CPUBINDING = (1UL<<4),
  HWLOC_TOPOLOGY_FLAG_RESTRICT_TO_MEMBINDING = (1UL<<5),
  HWLOC_TOPOLOGY_FLAG_DONT_CHANGE_BINDING = (1UL<<6),
  HWLOC_TOPOLOGY_FLAG_NO_DISTANCES = (1UL<<7),
  HWLOC_TOPOLOGY_FLAG_NO_MEMATTRS = (1UL<<8),
  HWLOC_TOPOLOGY_FLAG_NO_CPUKINDS = (1UL<<9)
};
objects.description: Flags configuring topology discovery/import behavior and constraints (include disallowed, assume thissystem, import support, restrictions, ignore features, etc.).
Bitfield-like report of what discovery information the backend could obtain (presence/counts, disallowed marking, CPU kind efficiency).
Bitfield-like report of supported CPU binding operations for the current topology/backend.
Bitfield-like report of supported memory binding features/policies and area operations.
Miscellaneous support flags; currently indicates whether support bits were imported from XML.
Aggregates pointers to support-description structures for discovery, cpubind, membind, and misc features.
Controls which object types are kept/filtered during discovery (all, none, structure-only, important).
Flags affecting behavior of topology restriction (remove CPU-less or mem-less objects, adapt misc/IO, nodeset mode).
Flags for changing sets of allowed PUs/NUMA nodes within a topology (all, local OS restrictions, custom).

Enumeration of flags accepted by the helper function hwloc_distrib(). Currently only HWLOC_DISTRIB_FLAG_REVERSE is defined to make distribution iterate from the last objects first. Intended to be OR'ed into the flags argument of hwloc_distrib().

Holds a square matrix of pairwise distances between a set of hwloc objects (objs). nbobjs is the number of objects. values is a flattened nbobjs*nbobjs matrix with element [i,j] at i*nbobjs+j. kind is a bitmask of hwloc_distances_kind_e describing provenance and value semantics. Callers may modify kind and the contents of objs and values, but must not replace or free the arrays themselves. Used by retrieval, transformation, and release APIs in this header.

Bitmask flags describing provenance and semantics of a distances matrix: FROM_OS or FROM_USER, exactly one VALUE_* (LATENCY, BANDWIDTH, or HOPS), and optionally HETEROGENEOUS_TYPES when objs contain mixed types.

Enumeration of in-place transformations that can be applied to a distances structure: remove NULL objs entries, convert bandwidth values to number of links, merge switch ports, or apply transitive closure to connect through switches.

objects.definition: typedef void * hwloc_distances_add_handle_t;
objects.description: Opaque handle used while constructing and committing a new distances structure via the add API. Created by hwloc_distances_add_create(), populated with hwloc_distances_add_values(), and finalized with hwloc_distances_add_commit().
Flags controlling behavior when committing a new distances structure: request grouping based on distances, optionally with relaxed accuracy.
Enumeration describing which single object attribute is changed in a diff entry: memory size, object name, or an info attribute value.

Union describing a single object-attribute modification within a diff. Variants: generic header; 64-bit integer attribute (optionally indexed) with old/new values; string attribute (optionally named) with old/new values.
Enumeration of top-level diff list element kinds: an object-attribute change or a marker that the difference was too complex to represent below a given object.

Union node used to build a singly-linked list of topology-diff elements. Variants include a generic header, an object-attribute diff (with object location info and an attribute-diff union), and a placeholder indicating the subtree diff was too complex. The typedef makes pointers to this union the public handle type for diff lists.
Bitflag enum controlling hwloc_topology_diff_apply(). Currently only allows applying a diff in reverse direction.

objects.definition:
enum hwloc_memattr_id_e {
  HWLOC_MEMATTR_ID_CAPACITY = 0,
  HWLOC_MEMATTR_ID_LOCALITY = 1,
  HWLOC_MEMATTR_ID_BANDWIDTH = 2,
  HWLOC_MEMATTR_ID_READ_BANDWIDTH = 4,
  HWLOC_MEMATTR_ID_WRITE_BANDWIDTH = 5,
  HWLOC_MEMATTR_ID_LATENCY = 3,
  HWLOC_MEMATTR_ID_READ_LATENCY = 6,
  HWLOC_MEMATTR_ID_WRITE_LATENCY = 7,
  HWLOC_MEMATTR_ID_MAX
};
objects.description: Enumeration of predefined memory attribute identifiers used by hwloc to reference built-in attributes such as capacity, bandwidth, and latency. Values are stable constants; HWLOC_MEMATTR_ID_MAX is a sentinel after which dynamically registered custom attributes start.

objects.definition: typedef unsigned hwloc_memattr_id_t;
objects.description: Typedef for a memory attribute identifier. Represents either a predefined attribute from enum hwloc_memattr_id_e or a custom attribute registered at runtime.
Enumeration indicating the kind of location used to describe an initiator: a cpuset or a specific topology object.

Structure describing where to measure memory attributes from (the initiator). It contains a type tag and a union holding either a cpuset or an object handle. The union members reference types from hwloc.h.
Flags controlling selection of NUMA nodes relative to a given locality when querying local NUMA nodes.
Flags describing memory attribute semantics: whether higher or lower values are preferred, and whether values depend on an initiator.

Forward-declared/externally-defined struct referenced for carrying arrays of info name/value attributes about CPU kinds. This header only references it in function prototypes (as pointer parameters) and does not define it here. Details of its fields and lifecycle are unknown from this header; consult the main hwloc headers for its definition.

objects.definition:
typedef struct hwloc_bitmap_s * hwloc_bitmap_t;
typedef const struct hwloc_bitmap_s * hwloc_const_bitmap_t;
objects.description: Opaque handle type to an internal bitmap object representing a (possibly infinite) set of non-negative integers. hwloc_bitmap_t is a pointer to an incomplete struct hwloc_bitmap_s; the actual struct definition is not present in this header. hwloc_const_bitmap_t is a const-qualified alias for read-only access to the same opaque type.

objects.definition: struct hwloc_bitmap_s;
objects.description: Incomplete/forward declaration for the internal bitmap structure. The concrete layout is intentionally hidden; users manipulate it through the hwloc_bitmap_t/const handle and bitmap API functions.
Bitmask flags controlling XML export behavior for hwloc topologies. Currently defines a flag to emit an XML format compatible with hwloc v2.x, possibly losing some details.

objects.definition:
enum hwloc_topology_export_synthetic_flags_e {
 /** \brief Export basic object types.
  *
  * Avoid recent/extended object types such as Die.
  * Rather export basic types such as Group that are supported
  * by all hwloc versions.
  * \hideinitializer
  */
 HWLOC_TOPOLOGY_EXPORT_SYNTHETIC_FLAG_NO_EXTENDED_TYPES = (1UL<<0),

 /** \brief Do not export level attributes.
  *
  * Ignore level attributes such as memory/cache sizes or PU indexes.
  * \hideinitializer
  */
 HWLOC_TOPOLOGY_EXPORT_SYNTHETIC_FLAG_NO_ATTRS = (1UL<<1),

 /** \brief Do not export memory information.
  *
  * Only export the actual hierarchy of normal CPU-side objects and ignore
  * where memory is attached.
  * This is useful for when the hierarchy of CPUs is what really matters,
  * but the exported topology will get a single machine-wide NUMA node.
  * \hideinitializer
  */
 HWLOC_TOPOLOGY_EXPORT_SYNTHETIC_FLAG_IGNORE_MEMORY = (1UL<<2)
};
objects.description: Bitmask flags that modify how a topology is exported as a synthetic description string. Options include avoiding extended object types, omitting level attributes, and ignoring memory placement.
Opaque topology handle typedef; only referenced here via macro renaming. This header does not provide its definition.
Opaque bitmap type representing a set of logical processors; only macro-renamed here. No definition provided in this header.
Opaque bitmap type representing a set of NUMA nodes; only macro-renamed here. No definition provided in this header.
Enumeration type for hwloc object kinds; only referenced via macro renaming here. Not defined in this header.
Enumeration describing cache type (data, instruction, unified). Only macro-renamed; no definition present here.
Enumeration describing bridge subtype (host, PCI). Only macro-renamed; no definition present here.
Enumeration/bitset describing OS device subtypes. Only referenced; not defined here.
Pointer/opaque to a topology object; only macro-renamed. No structure definition here.
Info key/value container structs used on objects; only names are macro-renamed here, definition not provided.
Union and attribute structs associated with objects. Only symbol names are provided here; no definitions are present in this header.
Enumeration of topology load/configuration flags. Only macro-renamed; not defined here.
Enumeration of component selection flags. Only referenced here; definition absent.
Enumeration of object type filtering policies. Only macro-renamed; not defined here.
Enumeration for topology restriction behavior. Only referenced; not defined here.
Enumeration for allowing objects/resources during restriction. Only referenced; not defined here.
Enumeration controlling object snprintf formatting. Only referenced; not defined here.
Enumeration for info list modification operations. Only referenced; not defined here.
Typedef for CPU binding flags (bitmask). Only macro-renamed; not defined here.
Enumeration/typedef for memory binding policy. Only referenced; definition absent.
Bitmask typedef for memory binding flags. Only referenced; definition absent.
Opaque bitmap type and its struct name; only renamed here. No definition present in this header.
Enumeration for distribution helper flags. Only referenced; not defined here.
Enumeration of memory attribute identifiers and its typedef. Only referenced; not defined here.
Location descriptor (object or cpuset) and related enum/union. Names are only macro-renamed; no definitions here.
Enumeration for selecting local NUMA nodes. Only referenced here; definition absent.
Enumeration for memory attribute flags. Only referenced; not defined here.
Enumeration controlling XML export. Only referenced; definition not present.
Enumeration controlling synthetic export. Only referenced; definition not present.
Distances matrix container struct. Only name is provided here; no definition included.
Enumeration describing distance kinds. Only referenced; not defined here.
Enumeration of possible transformations of distance matrices. Only referenced; not defined here.
Opaque handle used while adding distance matrices. Only referenced; no definition here.
Enumeration for topology diff object-attribute kinds. Only referenced; not defined here.
Enumeration for topology diff entry kinds. Only referenced; not defined here.
Types forming the topology diff representation (union, structs, typedef). Only names are macro-renamed here; no definitions in this header.
Enumeration/typedef of discovery phases. Only referenced; not defined here.
Discovery status struct and its flag enum. Only macro-renamed here; definitions missing.
Discovery component struct type. Only referenced; not defined here.
Backend instance struct type used by plugins. Only referenced here; definition not provided.
Enumeration/typedef of component types. Only referenced; not defined here.
Component descriptor struct. Only referenced; not defined here.

Discovery component descriptor. Describes a discovery provider (built-in or plugin) with its name, supported phases, exclusions, priority, default enablement, and an instantiate callback that creates a backend for a topology.
Bitmask enum of discovery phases performed by components/backends (global, CPU, memory, PCI, IO, misc, annotate, tweak).
Flags describing discovery status. Currently indicates whether allowed resources have been retrieved.
Runtime status communicated during discovery: current phase, dynamically excluded phases, and status flags.

Instance of a discovery component bound to a topology. Holds callbacks for discovery and teardown, phase mask, and flags. Private data may be allocated after the struct using HWLOC_BACKEND_PRIVATE_DATA.
Generic component type enumeration: discovery or XML.
Generic component container, with process-wide init/finalize, type, flags, and a data pointer to a specific component descriptor (e.g., hwloc_disc_component).

objects.definition: typedef void * hwloc_backend_distances_add_handle_t;
objects.description: Opaque handle used by backends while constructing and committing a distances structure during discovery.

functions.name: hwloc_get_api_version
functions.description: Return at runtime the hwloc API version the caller was built against. Usually equals HWLOC_API_VERSION when the runtime library matches the headers.

functions.name: hwloc_compare_types
functions.description: Compare two object types by their usual relative depth in a machine. Negative if type1 usually contains type2, positive if type1 is usually contained in type2, 0 if same, or HWLOC_TYPE_UNORDERED if incomparable.

functions.name: hwloc_topology_get_depth
functions.description: Return the number of normal levels in the topology (PU depth + 1). Memory/IO/Misc virtual levels are ignored.
requirements: topology must have been successfully loaded with hwloc_topology_load()

functions.name: hwloc_get_type_depth
functions.description: Return the depth index for objects of the given type, or a negative virtual depth for NUMA/IO/Misc types. Returns HWLOC_TYPE_DEPTH_UNKNOWN if absent, or HWLOC_TYPE_DEPTH_MULTIPLE for Groups when multiple Group levels exist.
requirements: topology must have been loaded with hwloc_topology_load()

functions.name: hwloc_get_type_depth_with_attr
functions.signature: int hwloc_get_type_depth_with_attr(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_obj_type_t type, union hwloc_obj_attr_u *attrp, size_t attrsize);
functions.description: Like hwloc_get_type_depth(), but may disambiguate multiple levels of the same type using attributes provided in attrp (e.g., Group depth). If attrp is NULL and attrsize is 0, behaves like hwloc_get_type_depth().
requirements: topology must be loaded
if attrp is non-NULL, attrsize should be >= sizeof(union hwloc_obj_attr_u) or large enough for provided fields

functions.name: hwloc_get_memory_parents_depth
functions.description: Return the normal (non-virtual) depth of the parents where Memory objects are attached if all have the same depth, or HWLOC_TYPE_DEPTH_MULTIPLE otherwise.
requirements: topology must be loaded

functions.name: hwloc_get_depth_type
functions.description: Return the object type present at the specified depth. Depth may be a normal depth [0..hwloc_topology_get_depth()-1] or a virtual depth (e.g., HWLOC_TYPE_DEPTH_NUMANODE).
requirements: topology must be loaded
depth must be valid; returns (hwloc_obj_type_t)-1 if not

functions.name: hwloc_get_nbobjs_by_depth
functions.description: Return the number of objects present at a given depth (0 if none).
requirements: topology must be loaded
depth must refer to an existing depth (normal or virtual)

functions.name: hwloc_get_obj_by_depth
functions.signature: hwloc_obj_t hwloc_get_obj_by_depth(hwloc_topology_t topology, int depth, unsigned idx) __hwloc_attribute_pure;
functions.description: Return the object at logical index idx on level depth, or NULL if out of range.
requirements: topology must be loaded
idx must be < hwloc_get_nbobjs_by_depth(topology, depth)

functions.name: hwloc_obj_type_string
functions.description: Return a constant string name for the given object type ("Unknown" if not recognized). Helpful for logging or parsing back with hwloc_type_sscanf().
requirements: Returned string must not be freed.

functions.name: hwloc_obj_type_snprintf
functions.signature: int hwloc_obj_type_snprintf(char * __hwloc_restrict string, size_t size, hwloc_obj_t obj, unsigned long flags);
functions.description: Format the type (and type-specific details) of obj into string. Output is consistent across a level and parseable by hwloc_type_sscanf() (unless SHORT_NAMES is used).
requirements: obj must be from a loaded topology
string may be NULL if size is 0
flags is an OR of hwloc_obj_snprintf_flag_e

functions.name: hwloc_obj_attr_snprintf
functions.signature: int hwloc_obj_attr_snprintf(char * __hwloc_restrict string, size_t size, hwloc_obj_t obj, const char * __hwloc_restrict separator, unsigned long flags);
functions.description: Format major attributes of obj (e.g., memory sizes, cache sizes) into string, separating fields by separator. Parseable by hwloc_type_sscanf() by default.
requirements: obj must be from a loaded topology
separator must be a valid C-string (non-NULL)
string may be NULL if size is 0
flags is an OR of hwloc_obj_snprintf_flag_e

functions.name: hwloc_type_sscanf
functions.signature: int hwloc_type_sscanf(const char *string, hwloc_obj_type_t *typep, union hwloc_obj_attr_u *attrp, size_t attrsize);
functions.description: Parse a type/attributes string (e.g., "L2Cache", "Group4", "OSDev:GPU") into a type and optional attributes. Attributes not present are set to -1 (or 0 for OS device type).
requirements: string and typep must be non-NULL
if attrp is non-NULL, attrsize should be >= sizeof(union hwloc_obj_attr_u) to fill all attributes
Matching is case-insensitive and may use prefixes

functions.name: hwloc_modify_infos
functions.signature: int hwloc_modify_infos(struct hwloc_infos_s *infos, unsigned long operation, const char *name, const char *value);
functions.description: Add, add-unique, replace, or remove name/value info pairs in an infos array according to operation. Strings are copied internally.
requirements: infos must be a valid infos structure
For ADD/ADD_UNIQUE/REPLACE: name and value must be non-NULL
For REMOVE: name and/or value may be NULL to match all by the other or remove all if both NULL

functions.name: hwloc_topology_get_infos
functions.description: Return a pointer to the topology-wide infos structure (discovery and OS information). The pointer is owned by hwloc and must not be freed or modified directly.
requirements: topology must be initialized (preferably loaded)
Returned pointer must not be freed or modified

functions.name: hwloc_obj_set_subtype
functions.signature: int hwloc_obj_set_subtype(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_obj_t obj, const char *subtype);
functions.description: Set or replace the subtype string of obj (copied internally). Use to label user-added objects such as Groups.
requirements: obj must belong to topology
subtype may be NULL to remove existing subtype
May fail with ENOMEM if allocation fails

functions.name: hwloc_set_cpubind
functions.signature: int hwloc_set_cpubind(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_const_cpuset_t set, int flags);
functions.description: Bind the current process or thread to the given physical CPU set. Honors flags such as PROCESS, THREAD, STRICT, NOMEMBIND.
requirements: topology should correspond to this system if real binding is desired (or set IS_THISSYSTEM flag)
set must be a valid cpuset; consider hwloc_bitmap_singlify() on OSes that only allow single CPU
flags is an OR of hwloc_cpubind_flags_t; THREAD and PROCESS are mutually exclusive
May fail with ENOSYS (unsupported) or EXDEV (cannot enforce)

functions.name: hwloc_get_cpubind
functions.signature: int hwloc_get_cpubind(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_cpuset_t set, int flags);
functions.description: Retrieve the binding of the current process or thread into set (the last set it was bound to).
requirements: set must be allocated by caller
flags may include PROCESS or THREAD (mutually exclusive) and optionally STRICT for process-wide uniformity check
topology should match this system if querying via OS hooks

functions.name: hwloc_set_proc_cpubind
functions.signature: int hwloc_set_proc_cpubind(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_pid_t pid, hwloc_const_cpuset_t set, int flags);
functions.description: Bind the specified process (or on Linux, a thread when THREAD is passed and pid is a TID) to the given CPU set.
requirements: pid must refer to a valid process (or thread ID on Linux with THREAD)
flags may include THREAD only on Linux; not allowed on non-Linux
May fail with ENOSYS/EXDEV

functions.name: hwloc_get_proc_cpubind
functions.signature: int hwloc_get_proc_cpubind(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_pid_t pid, hwloc_cpuset_t set, int flags);
functions.description: Get the binding of the specified process (or thread on Linux with THREAD) into set.
requirements: set must be allocated by caller
flags may include THREAD only on Linux; not allowed on non-Linux
May fail with ENOSYS

functions.name: hwloc_set_thread_cpubind
functions.signature: int hwloc_set_thread_cpubind(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_thread_t thread, hwloc_const_cpuset_t set, int flags);
functions.description: Bind the given thread to the specified CPU set.
requirements: Only available when hwloc_thread_t is defined on the platform (pthread_t on Unix, HANDLE on Windows)
flags must not include HWLOC_CPUBIND_PROCESS
set must be a valid cpuset

functions.name: hwloc_get_thread_cpubind
functions.signature: int hwloc_get_thread_cpubind(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_thread_t thread, hwloc_cpuset_t set, int flags);
functions.description: Get the CPU binding of the specified thread into set.
requirements: Only available when hwloc_thread_t is defined on the platform
flags must not include HWLOC_CPUBIND_PROCESS
set must be allocated by caller

functions.name: hwloc_get_last_cpu_location
functions.signature: int hwloc_get_last_cpu_location(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_cpuset_t set, int flags);
functions.description: Fill set with PUs on which the current process or thread last ran. May already be outdated due to migration.
requirements: set must be allocated by caller
flags may include PROCESS or THREAD (or 0 for single-threaded convenience)

functions.name: hwloc_get_proc_last_cpu_location
functions.signature: int hwloc_get_proc_last_cpu_location(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_pid_t pid, hwloc_cpuset_t set, int flags);
functions.description: Fill set with PUs on which the specified process (or thread on Linux if THREAD passed and pid is a TID) last ran.
requirements: set must be allocated by caller
flags may include THREAD on Linux only

functions.name: hwloc_set_membind
functions.signature: int hwloc_set_membind(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_const_bitmap_t set, hwloc_membind_policy_t policy, int flags);
functions.description: Set the default memory binding policy of the current process or thread to prefer the nodes in set according to policy. set is a cpuset by default or a nodeset if BYNODESET is passed.
requirements: set must be a valid bitmap (cpuset or nodeset per flags)
flags is an OR of hwloc_membind_flags_t; PROCESS and THREAD are mutually exclusive
STRICT may cause failure if the policy cannot be enforced
May fail with ENOSYS/EXDEV

functions.name: hwloc_get_membind
functions.signature: int hwloc_get_membind(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_bitmap_t set, hwloc_membind_policy_t * policy, int flags);
functions.description: Query the default memory binding policy and locality of the current process or thread. Returns set (union or strict view) and policy (or MIXED).
requirements: set must be allocated by caller
policy must be non-NULL
flags may include PROCESS or THREAD (mutually exclusive); STRICT only meaningful with PROCESS
BYNODESET switches set interpretation to nodeset
Invalid flags cause -1/EINVAL

functions.name: hwloc_set_proc_membind
functions.signature: int hwloc_set_proc_membind(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_pid_t pid, hwloc_const_bitmap_t set, hwloc_membind_policy_t policy, int flags);
functions.description: Set the default memory binding policy for the specified process.
requirements: set is cpuset by default, nodeset with BYNODESET flag
flags must not include THREAD (nonsensical for this call)
May fail with ENOSYS/EXDEV

functions.name: hwloc_get_proc_membind
functions.signature: int hwloc_get_proc_membind(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_pid_t pid, hwloc_bitmap_t set, hwloc_membind_policy_t * policy, int flags);
functions.description: Query default memory binding policy/locality of the specified process. Can OR sets across threads or require STRICT uniformity.
requirements: set must be allocated by caller; policy must be non-NULL
flags may include PROCESS; THREAD is not meaningful and should not be used
BYNODESET switches to nodeset
Invalid flags cause -1/EINVAL

functions.name: hwloc_set_area_membind
functions.signature: int hwloc_set_area_membind(hwloc_topology_t topology, const void *addr, size_t len, hwloc_const_bitmap_t set, hwloc_membind_policy_t policy, int flags);
functions.description: Bind the already-allocated memory range [addr, addr+len) to the specified nodes according to policy. set is cpuset by default or nodeset with BYNODESET.
requirements: addr must be a valid pointer; len may be 0 (success)
set must be valid (cpuset/nodeset per flags)
STRICT may cause failure; may fail with ENOSYS/EXDEV

functions.name: hwloc_get_area_membind
functions.signature: int hwloc_get_area_membind(hwloc_topology_t topology, const void *addr, size_t len, hwloc_bitmap_t set, hwloc_membind_policy_t * policy, int flags);
functions.description: Query the binding policy and locality for pages covering [addr, addr+len). With STRICT, require identical policy/nodes across all pages; otherwise union and possibly MIXED policy.
requirements: addr must be valid; len must be > 0 or returns -1/EINVAL
set must be allocated; policy must be non-NULL
BYNODESET switches to nodeset
Invalid flags cause -1/EINVAL

functions.name: hwloc_get_area_memlocation
functions.signature: int hwloc_get_area_memlocation(hwloc_topology_t topology, const void *addr, size_t len, hwloc_bitmap_t set, int flags);
functions.description: Return the NUMA nodes (or CPUs if not BYNODESET) where pages in [addr, addr+len) are physically allocated. May be empty if pages not yet allocated. Snapshot can be outdated.
requirements: set must be allocated; addr valid
If len is 0, set is emptied and 0 is returned
BYNODESET in flags makes set a nodeset

functions.name: hwloc_alloc
functions.description: Allocate page-aligned memory from the OS (similar to malloc but tries for page alignment). Free with hwloc_free().
requirements: len may be any size; returns NULL on error
Must be freed with hwloc_free(topology, ptr, len)

functions.name: hwloc_alloc_membind
functions.signature: void * hwloc_alloc_membind(hwloc_topology_t topology, size_t len, hwloc_const_bitmap_t set, hwloc_membind_policy_t policy, int flags) __hwloc_attribute_malloc;
functions.description: Allocate memory and attempt to bind it to nodes per set and policy. Returns NULL with errno set (ENOSYS/EXDEV/ENOMEM) on failure cases described.
requirements: set must be valid (cpuset by default, nodeset with BYNODESET)
STRICT affects failure behavior
Free with hwloc_free()

functions.name: hwloc_free
functions.signature: int hwloc_free(hwloc_topology_t topology, void *addr, size_t len);
functions.description: Free memory previously allocated by hwloc_alloc() or hwloc_alloc_membind().
requirements: addr must have been returned by hwloc_alloc or hwloc_alloc_membind
len should match the allocation size

functions.name: hwloc_topology_set_pid
functions.description: Change the process whose view of the system is used for discovery (e.g., allowed CPUs). PID is only used at load time; if the process exits or PID is reused, the corresponding view is used.
requirements: Must be called after hwloc_topology_init() and before hwloc_topology_load()
May return -1/ENOSYS on unsupported platforms

functions.name: hwloc_topology_set_synthetic
functions.description: Select the synthetic discovery backend with the given description string (e.g., "2 4 2" or typed levels). Does not load; call hwloc_topology_load() later.
requirements: Must be called between hwloc_topology_init() and hwloc_topology_load()
description must be a valid synthetic description; invalid returns -1/EINVAL

functions.name: hwloc_topology_set_xml
functions.signature: int hwloc_topology_set_xml(hwloc_topology_t __hwloc_restrict topology, const char * __hwloc_restrict xmlpath);
functions.description: Select the XML-file discovery backend using the file at xmlpath. Does not load; call hwloc_topology_load().
requirements: Must be called before hwloc_topology_load()
xmlpath must point to a readable valid XML file; returns -1/EINVAL on failure
Set IS_THISSYSTEM flag to enable real binding hooks if needed

functions.name: hwloc_topology_set_xmlbuffer
functions.signature: int hwloc_topology_set_xmlbuffer(hwloc_topology_t __hwloc_restrict topology, const char * __hwloc_restrict buffer, int size);
functions.description: Select the XML-memory-buffer discovery backend using buffer of given size (including terminating NUL). Call hwloc_topology_load() to load.
requirements: Must be called before hwloc_topology_load()
buffer must contain valid XML; returns -1/EINVAL on parse/read failure
size must include the ending '\0'

functions.name: hwloc_topology_set_components
functions.signature: int hwloc_topology_set_components(hwloc_topology_t __hwloc_restrict topology, unsigned long flags, const char * __hwloc_restrict name);
functions.description: Prevent a discovery component (e.g., "cuda", optionally with phase suffix) from being used when loading this topology. Typically use HWLOC_TOPOLOGY_COMPONENTS_FLAG_BLACKLIST.
requirements: Must be called before hwloc_topology_load()
flags must be HWLOC_TOPOLOGY_COMPONENTS_FLAG_BLACKLIST
name must be a valid component (e.g., "linux:io", "cuda")

functions.name: hwloc_topology_set_flags
functions.signature: int hwloc_topology_set_flags(hwloc_topology_t topology, unsigned long flags);
functions.description: Set OR'ed topology flags (e.g., INCLUDE_DISALLOWED, IS_THISSYSTEM, RESTRICT_TO_CPUBINDING) to control discovery and behavior. Overwrites previous flags.
requirements: Must be called before hwloc_topology_load()
flags must be a valid OR of hwloc_topology_flags_e

functions.name: hwloc_topology_get_flags
functions.description: Return the OR'ed topology flags set on topology (0 if none). Can be called before or after load.

functions.name: hwloc_topology_is_thissystem
functions.description: Return 1 if the topology was built from the running system (or IS_THISSYSTEM asserted), 0 otherwise (XML/synthetic/other roots).

functions.name: hwloc_topology_get_support
functions.description: Return a pointer to a structure describing what discovery/cpubind/membind/misc features are supported for this topology.
requirements: The returned pointer is owned by hwloc; do not free or modify
Valid only after discovery (after hwloc_topology_load()) for accurate values

functions.name: hwloc_topology_set_type_filter
functions.signature: int hwloc_topology_set_type_filter(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_obj_type_t type, enum hwloc_type_filter_e filter);
functions.description: Set filtering policy for a specific type (KEEP_ALL/KEEP_NONE/KEEP_STRUCTURE/KEEP_IMPORTANT). Controls which objects of that type are kept in the topology.
requirements: Must be called before hwloc_topology_load()
Some types may not support certain filters (errors -1)

functions.name: hwloc_topology_get_type_filter
functions.signature: int hwloc_topology_get_type_filter(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_obj_type_t type, enum hwloc_type_filter_e *filter);
functions.description: Get the current filtering policy for a specific type.
requirements: filter must be non-NULL

functions.name: hwloc_topology_set_all_types_filter
functions.description: Set the same filtering policy on all object types (unsupported types silently ignored).
requirements: Must be called before hwloc_topology_load()

functions.name: hwloc_topology_set_cache_types_filter
functions.description: Set filtering policy for all CPU cache types (not memory-side caches).
requirements: Must be called before hwloc_topology_load()

functions.name: hwloc_topology_set_icache_types_filter
functions.description: Set filtering policy for all CPU instruction cache object types.
requirements: Must be called before hwloc_topology_load()

functions.name: hwloc_topology_set_io_types_filter
functions.description: Set filtering policy for all I/O object types.
requirements: Must be called before hwloc_topology_load()

functions.name: hwloc_topology_set_userdata
functions.description: Associate an application-defined userdata pointer with the topology. Not exported to XML. hwloc never modifies it.
requirements: Call after init and before destroy; value may be NULL

functions.name: hwloc_topology_get_userdata
functions.description: Retrieve the application-defined userdata pointer previously set with hwloc_topology_set_userdata().

functions.name: hwloc_topology_restrict
functions.signature: int hwloc_topology_restrict(hwloc_topology_t __hwloc_restrict topology, hwloc_const_bitmap_t set, unsigned long flags);
functions.description: Restrict the topology to the given CPU set by default or to a nodeset with BYNODESET. Removes objects outside and updates sets accordingly; may reorder objects and change logical indexes.
requirements: topology must be loaded
set must be a valid CPU set or nodeset
flags is an OR of hwloc_restrict_flags_e; BYNODESET may not be combined with REMOVE_CPULESS; REMOVE_MEMLESS only with BYNODESET
On ENOMEM, topology is reinitialized and must be reloaded or destroyed

functions.name: hwloc_topology_allow
functions.signature: int hwloc_topology_allow(hwloc_topology_t __hwloc_restrict topology, hwloc_const_cpuset_t cpuset, hwloc_const_nodeset_t nodeset, unsigned long flags);
functions.description: Change the sets of allowed PUs and NUMA nodes (requires topology built with INCLUDE_DISALLOWED). Does not remove objects; only changes allowed sets reported by topology getters.
requirements: Topology must have been built with HWLOC_TOPOLOGY_FLAG_INCLUDE_DISALLOWED
flags must be exactly one of HWLOC_ALLOW_FLAG_ALL, HWLOC_ALLOW_FLAG_LOCAL_RESTRICTIONS, or HWLOC_ALLOW_FLAG_CUSTOM
For ALL/LOCAL_RESTRICTIONS, cpuset and nodeset must be NULL
For CUSTOM, provide cpuset and/or nodeset

functions.name: hwloc_topology_insert_misc_object
functions.signature: hwloc_obj_t hwloc_topology_insert_misc_object(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_obj_t parent, const char *name);
functions.description: Insert a new Misc object as a leaf under parent (no cpuset). Useful for annotations (e.g., DIMM, custom tags). Returns NULL if filtered-out or on error.
requirements: parent must be a valid object in topology
name should be unique among Misc objects; string is duplicated
Fails/returns NULL if Misc objects are filtered (KEEP_NONE)
Non-printable chars in name are dropped when exporting to XML

functions.name: hwloc_topology_alloc_group_object
functions.description: Allocate a Group object to later insert for adding hierarchy. Caller must initialize at least one of its sets (cpu/nodeset) before insertion or free it if not inserting.
requirements: Use with the same topology for insert/free
Initialize cpuset and/or nodeset (or complete_* variants) before insertion

functions.name: hwloc_topology_free_group_object
functions.description: Free a Group object previously allocated with hwloc_topology_alloc_group_object() and not inserted.
requirements: group must have been allocated for the same topology
Only use if not passed to hwloc_topology_insert_group_object()

functions.name: hwloc_topology_insert_group_object
functions.description: Insert a prepared Group object to add structure (e.g., grouping siblings). May insert a new level or merge/discard if redundant or conflicting. Returns the inserted or existing object, or NULL on failure.
requirements: group must have non-empty cpuset and/or nodeset (or complete_* equivalents) identifying objects to group; sets larger than topology are silently restricted
May reorder objects and change logical indexes
If insertion fails (conflicts or filtered-out), the group object is freed

functions.name: hwloc_obj_add_other_obj_sets
functions.description: OR src sets into dst, allocating dst sets as needed. Useful to build Group sets before insertion by aggregating children.
requirements: dst and src must be valid objects
May fail with ENOMEM

functions.name: hwloc_topology_refresh
functions.description: Refresh internal caches after modifying the topology (restriction, insertions, distances/memattrs changes). Helps end a non-thread-safe modification phase.
requirements: Call after all unsafe modifications and before concurrent read-only access from multiple threads

functions.name: hwloc_topology_init
functions.description: Allocate and initialize a new topology context. Must be followed by configuration (optional) and hwloc_topology_load().
requirements: topologyp must be non-NULL; receives new context on success

functions.name: hwloc_topology_load
functions.description: Discover and build the topology into the context after optional pre-load configuration. May only be called once. On failure, the topology is reinitialized.
requirements: topology must be created by hwloc_topology_init()
Must be called exactly once per topology
No other routine may be called earlier using this topology (except configuration/setsource)

functions.name: hwloc_topology_destroy
functions.description: Terminate and free a topology context and all associated resources.
requirements: topology must have been initialized; safe to call whether load succeeded or not

functions.name: hwloc_topology_dup
functions.description: Duplicate an entire topology (objects and structure) into a new context. Object userdata pointers are not duplicated (both topologies point to same userdata).
requirements: oldtopology must be a valid topology (typically loaded)
newtopology must be non-NULL

functions.name: hwloc_topology_abi_check
functions.description: Verify that the topology is compatible with the current hwloc library/component ABI. Returns 0 if compatible, -1/EINVAL if not.
requirements: topology must be valid (typically loaded)

functions.name: hwloc_topology_check
functions.description: Run internal consistency checks on the topology and abort the program if inconsistencies are detected. Developer tool.
requirements: Only useful for debugging/development
topology should have been loaded

functions.name: hwloc_get_nbobjs_by_type
functions.description: Return the number of objects of the given type, or -1 if multiple levels exist for that type (e.g., Group), or 0 if none.
requirements: topology must be loaded

functions.name: hwloc_get_root_obj
functions.description: Return the root object (type HWLOC_OBJ_MACHINE). Never returns NULL.
requirements: topology must be loaded

functions.name: hwloc_get_obj_by_type
functions.signature: hwloc_obj_t hwloc_get_obj_by_type(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_obj_type_t type, unsigned idx) __hwloc_attribute_pure;
functions.description: Return the object of given type at logical index idx, or NULL if none or if multiple levels exist for that type.
requirements: topology must be loaded
idx must be < count returned by hwloc_get_nbobjs_by_type()

functions.name: hwloc_get_next_obj_by_depth
functions.signature: hwloc_obj_t hwloc_get_next_obj_by_depth(hwloc_topology_t topology, int depth, hwloc_obj_t prev);
functions.description: Iterate objects at a given depth. Pass NULL to get the first object; then pass previous result to get the next; NULL when done.
requirements: topology must be loaded
depth must be valid

functions.name: hwloc_get_next_obj_by_type
functions.signature: hwloc_obj_t hwloc_get_next_obj_by_type(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_obj_type_t type, hwloc_obj_t prev);
functions.description: Iterate objects of a given type. Returns NULL if multiple levels exist for the type (e.g., Group).
requirements: topology must be loaded

functions.name: hwloc_obj_get_info_by_name
functions.signature: const char * hwloc_obj_get_info_by_name(hwloc_obj_t obj, const char *name) __hwloc_attribute_pure;
functions.description: Search obj->infos for the first pair with the given name and return its value, or NULL if none.
requirements: obj must be valid
Returned string is owned by hwloc and must not be freed

functions.name: hwloc_get_info_by_name
functions.signature: const char * hwloc_get_info_by_name(struct hwloc_infos_s *infos, const char *name) __hwloc_attribute_pure;
functions.description: Search the given infos array for the first attribute with the given name and return its value, or NULL if none.
requirements: infos must be valid
Returned string is owned by hwloc and must not be freed

functions.name: hwloc_obj_add_info
functions.signature: int hwloc_obj_add_info(hwloc_obj_t obj, const char *name, const char *value);
functions.description: Append a name/value info pair to obj->infos (even if a same-name pair exists). Strings are copied internally.
requirements: obj must be valid
name and value must be non-NULL
If value contains non-printable characters, they will be dropped when exporting to XML

functions.name: hwloc_alloc_membind_policy
functions.signature: void * hwloc_alloc_membind_policy(hwloc_topology_t topology, size_t len, hwloc_const_bitmap_t set, hwloc_membind_policy_t policy, int flags) __hwloc_attribute_malloc;
functions.description: Allocate memory bound to nodes per set/policy by first trying hwloc_alloc_membind(), then falling back to temporarily changing the current (thread/process) membind policy before allocating.
requirements: set must be valid (cpuset by default, nodeset with BYNODESET)
May change the current memory binding policy as a side effect
Free with hwloc_free()

functions.name: hwloc_get_type_or_below_depth
functions.description: Return the depth of objects of the given normal type, or if absent, the depth of the first present type typically found inside it. For memory/IO/Misc types, returns their virtual depth.
requirements: topology must be loaded

functions.name: hwloc_get_type_or_above_depth
functions.description: Return the depth of objects of the given normal type, or if absent, the depth of the first present type typically containing it. For memory/IO/Misc types, returns their virtual depth.
requirements: topology must be loaded

functions.name: hwloc_obj_type_is_normal
functions.description: Returns 1 if the given hwloc object type is a Normal object (part of the main CPU hierarchy), 0 otherwise. Excludes NUMA nodes, I/O, and Misc objects. Used to classify object kinds.
requirements: Argument type must be a valid hwloc_obj_type_t.

functions.name: hwloc_obj_type_is_io
functions.description: Returns 1 if the type is an I/O object (bridges, PCI devices, OS devices), 0 otherwise.
requirements: Argument type must be a valid hwloc_obj_type_t.

functions.name: hwloc_obj_type_is_memory
functions.description: Returns 1 if the type is a Memory object (NUMA nodes, memory-side caches), 0 otherwise.
requirements: Argument type must be a valid hwloc_obj_type_t.

functions.name: hwloc_obj_type_is_cache
functions.description: Returns 1 if the type is a CPU cache (Data, Unified, or Instruction cache). Memory-side caches are excluded.
requirements: Argument type must be a valid hwloc_obj_type_t.

functions.name: hwloc_obj_type_is_dcache
functions.description: Returns 1 if the type is a CPU Data or Unified cache. Memory-side caches are excluded.
requirements: Argument type must be a valid hwloc_obj_type_t.

functions.name: hwloc_obj_type_is_icache
functions.description: Returns 1 if the type is a CPU Instruction cache. Memory-side caches are excluded.
requirements: Argument type must be a valid hwloc_obj_type_t.

functions.name: hwloc_get_first_largest_obj_inside_cpuset
functions.description: Finds the first object that is included in the given cpuset while its parent is not, i.e., a largest object fully contained within the set. Useful for iterating largest covering objects.
requirements: topology must be a valid, initialized hwloc_topology_t.
set must be a valid cpuset; if it does not intersect the root cpuset, NULL is returned.
Objects with empty CPU sets are naturally ignored by the inclusion checks in the implementation.

functions.name: hwloc_get_largest_objs_inside_cpuset
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_get_largest_objs_inside_cpuset(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_const_cpuset_t set, hwloc_obj_t * __hwloc_restrict objs, int max);
functions.description: Fills objs with up to max objects that form the set of largest objects whose union exactly covers the given cpuset. Returns the number found, or -1 if no such set exists.
requirements: topology must be a valid, initialized hwloc_topology_t.
set must be a valid cpuset.
objs must be a valid array of hwloc_obj_t pointers of length at least max.
max must be a non-negative integer.

functions.name: hwloc_get_next_obj_inside_cpuset_by_depth
functions.signature: static __hwloc_inline hwloc_obj_t hwloc_get_next_obj_inside_cpuset_by_depth(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_const_cpuset_t set, int depth, hwloc_obj_t prev);
functions.description: Iterates over objects at a given depth that are included in the cpuset. Pass NULL prev for the first match; subsequent calls pass the previous return value.
requirements: topology must be valid.
set must be a valid cpuset.
depth must refer to a level where objects have CPU sets (not I/O or Misc).
Objects with empty CPU sets are ignored.

functions.name: hwloc_get_next_obj_inside_cpuset_by_type
functions.signature: static __hwloc_inline hwloc_obj_t hwloc_get_next_obj_inside_cpuset_by_type(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_const_cpuset_t set, hwloc_obj_type_t type, hwloc_obj_t prev);
functions.description: Iterates over objects of a given type that are included in the cpuset. Returns NULL if the type has unknown or multiple depths; in that case, use the depth-based variant.
requirements: topology must be valid.
set must be a valid cpuset.
type must correspond to a unique depth and to objects with CPU sets (not I/O or Misc).
Objects with empty CPU sets are ignored.

functions.name: hwloc_get_obj_inside_cpuset_by_depth
functions.signature: static __hwloc_inline hwloc_obj_t hwloc_get_obj_inside_cpuset_by_depth(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_const_cpuset_t set, int depth, unsigned idx) __hwloc_attribute_pure;
functions.description: Returns the idx-th object at the specified depth that is included in the cpuset, or NULL if none.
requirements: topology must be valid.
set must be a valid cpuset.
depth must refer to a level with objects that have CPU sets (not I/O or Misc).
Objects with empty CPU sets are ignored.
idx is a zero-based logical index among those included in the set.

functions.name: hwloc_get_obj_inside_cpuset_by_type
functions.signature: static __hwloc_inline hwloc_obj_t hwloc_get_obj_inside_cpuset_by_type(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_const_cpuset_t set, hwloc_obj_type_t type, unsigned idx) __hwloc_attribute_pure;
functions.description: Returns the idx-th object of the specified type included in the cpuset, or NULL. If the type maps to multiple depths, the caller should use the depth-based variant.
requirements: topology must be valid.
set must be a valid cpuset.
type must correspond to a unique depth and to objects with CPU sets.
Objects with empty CPU sets are ignored.
idx is zero-based among those included in the set.

functions.name: hwloc_get_nbobjs_inside_cpuset_by_depth
functions.signature: static __hwloc_inline unsigned hwloc_get_nbobjs_inside_cpuset_by_depth(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_const_cpuset_t set, int depth) __hwloc_attribute_pure;
functions.description: Counts objects at a given depth whose CPU sets are included in the specified cpuset.
requirements: topology must be valid.
set must be a valid cpuset.
depth must refer to a level with objects that have CPU sets (not I/O or Misc).
Objects with empty CPU sets are ignored.

functions.name: hwloc_get_nbobjs_inside_cpuset_by_type
functions.signature: static __hwloc_inline int hwloc_get_nbobjs_inside_cpuset_by_type(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_const_cpuset_t set, hwloc_obj_type_t type) __hwloc_attribute_pure;
functions.description: Returns the number of objects of a given type included in the cpuset. Returns 0 if the type is absent; returns -1 if there are multiple levels of that type.
requirements: topology must be valid.
set must be a valid cpuset.
type must correspond to objects with CPU sets (not I/O).
Objects with empty CPU sets are ignored.

functions.name: hwloc_get_obj_index_inside_cpuset
functions.signature: static __hwloc_inline int hwloc_get_obj_index_inside_cpuset(hwloc_topology_t topology __hwloc_attribute_unused, hwloc_const_cpuset_t set, hwloc_obj_t obj) __hwloc_attribute_pure;
functions.description: Returns the logical index of obj among objects at the same level that are included in the cpuset, or -1 if obj is not included.
requirements: set must be a valid cpuset.
obj must have a non-empty CPU set and be included in set for a non-negative result.
This function cannot work if obj does not have a CPU set (I/O objects).

functions.name: hwloc_get_child_covering_cpuset
functions.signature: static __hwloc_inline hwloc_obj_t hwloc_get_child_covering_cpuset(hwloc_topology_t topology __hwloc_attribute_unused, hwloc_const_cpuset_t set, hwloc_obj_t parent) __hwloc_attribute_pure;
functions.description: Returns the child of parent whose cpuset fully includes the given set. Returns NULL if none or if the set is empty.
requirements: set must be a valid, non-empty cpuset.
parent must have a CPU set (not an I/O or Misc object).
Children are scanned among normal children first, then memory/I/O/Misc.

functions.name: hwloc_get_obj_covering_cpuset
functions.description: Returns the lowest object whose cpuset fully covers the given set, or NULL if set is empty or not included in the topology root cpuset.
requirements: topology must be valid.
set must be a valid cpuset that is included in the root object's cpuset and not empty.

functions.name: hwloc_get_next_obj_covering_cpuset_by_depth
functions.signature: static __hwloc_inline hwloc_obj_t hwloc_get_next_obj_covering_cpuset_by_depth(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_const_cpuset_t set, int depth, hwloc_obj_t prev);
functions.description: Iterates over objects at a given depth whose cpusets intersect the specified cpuset. Pass NULL prev for the first, otherwise pass the previous object.
requirements: topology must be valid.
set must be a valid cpuset.
depth must refer to a level where objects have CPU sets (not I/O or Misc).

functions.name: hwloc_get_next_obj_covering_cpuset_by_type
functions.signature: static __hwloc_inline hwloc_obj_t hwloc_get_next_obj_covering_cpuset_by_type(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_const_cpuset_t set, hwloc_obj_type_t type, hwloc_obj_t prev);
functions.description: Iterates over objects of the given type whose cpusets intersect the cpuset. Returns NULL if the type has unknown or multiple depths; use the depth-based variant then.
requirements: topology must be valid.
set must be a valid cpuset.
type must correspond to a unique depth and to objects with CPU sets.

functions.name: hwloc_get_ancestor_obj_by_depth
functions.signature: static __hwloc_inline hwloc_obj_t hwloc_get_ancestor_obj_by_depth(hwloc_topology_t topology __hwloc_attribute_unused, int depth, hwloc_obj_t obj) __hwloc_attribute_pure;
functions.description: Returns the ancestor of obj at the given depth, or NULL if none (e.g., if obj is shallower than depth). Intended for intermediate levels (not PU/NUMA).
requirements: obj must be a valid object in the topology.
depth should refer to an intermediate level (not PU or NUMA) for meaningful results.

functions.name: hwloc_get_ancestor_obj_by_type
functions.signature: static __hwloc_inline hwloc_obj_t hwloc_get_ancestor_obj_by_type(hwloc_topology_t topology __hwloc_attribute_unused, hwloc_obj_type_t type, hwloc_obj_t obj) __hwloc_attribute_pure;
functions.description: Returns the lowest ancestor of obj with the specified type, or NULL if none. Not intended for PU or NUMA types.
requirements: obj must be a valid object.
type should be an intermediate type (e.g., PACKAGE, CORE, CACHE), not PU or NUMANODE.

functions.name: hwloc_get_common_ancestor_obj
functions.signature: static __hwloc_inline hwloc_obj_t hwloc_get_common_ancestor_obj(hwloc_topology_t topology __hwloc_attribute_unused, hwloc_obj_t obj1, hwloc_obj_t obj2) __hwloc_attribute_pure;
functions.description: Returns the lowest common ancestor of obj1 and obj2. This function never returns NULL.
requirements: obj1 and obj2 must be valid objects from the same topology.

functions.name: hwloc_obj_is_in_subtree
functions.signature: static __hwloc_inline int hwloc_obj_is_in_subtree(hwloc_topology_t topology __hwloc_attribute_unused, hwloc_obj_t obj, hwloc_obj_t subtree_root) __hwloc_attribute_pure;
functions.description: Returns 1 if obj is within the subtree rooted at subtree_root (via cpuset inclusion), 0 otherwise.
requirements: obj and subtree_root must have non-NULL CPU sets (not I/O or Misc).

functions.name: hwloc_get_next_child
functions.signature: static __hwloc_inline hwloc_obj_t hwloc_get_next_child(hwloc_topology_t topology __hwloc_attribute_unused, hwloc_obj_t parent, hwloc_obj_t prev);
functions.description: Returns the next child of parent, iterating across normal, then memory, then I/O, then Misc child lists. Pass NULL prev for the first child.
requirements: parent must be a valid object.
prev must be NULL for the first call, or one of parent's children for subsequent calls.

functions.name: hwloc_get_cache_type_depth
functions.signature: static __hwloc_inline int hwloc_get_cache_type_depth(hwloc_topology_t topology, unsigned cachelevel, hwloc_obj_cache_type_t cachetype);
functions.description: Finds the depth of cache objects matching the given cache level and type. May return the depth of a unified cache when matching instruction/data types. Returns HWLOC_TYPE_DEPTH_MULTIPLE when ambiguous, or HWLOC_TYPE_DEPTH_UNKNOWN if no match.
requirements: topology must be valid.
cachelevel is the cache level (e.g., 1 for L1).
cachetype may be a specific type or (hwloc_obj_cache_type_t)-1 to accept any at that level.

functions.name: hwloc_get_cache_covering_cpuset
functions.description: Returns the lowest data (or unified) cache whose cpuset covers the given cpuset, searching upward from the lowest covering object.
requirements: topology must be valid.
set must be a valid cpuset.
Returns NULL if no such cache exists.

functions.name: hwloc_get_shared_cache_covering_obj
functions.description: Returns the first data (or unified) cache above obj that is shared with at least one other PU (i.e., cache cpuset != obj cpuset). Returns NULL for invalid objects (e.g., no cpuset) or if none.
requirements: obj must have a non-NULL cpuset.
obj should be a normal object; I/O objects yield NULL.

functions.name: hwloc_bitmap_singlify_per_core
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_bitmap_singlify_per_core(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_bitmap_t cpuset, unsigned which);
functions.description: For each core, if cpuset contains some of its PUs, keep only a single PU per core according to 'which' (0 keeps the first PU that was originally set; otherwise selects the PU at index 'which' among those originally set). Returns 0.
requirements: topology must be valid.
cpuset must be a valid, mutable bitmap.
which selects among PUs of a core that were originally set; if which exceeds their count for a core, that core retains no PU.
PUs not below a Core object are ignored and not removed.

functions.name: hwloc_get_pu_obj_by_os_index
functions.description: Returns the PU object with the given OS index, or NULL if none. Useful to map cpuset bit indexes to PU objects.
requirements: topology must be valid.
os_index is an OS CPU identifier present in the topology.

functions.name: hwloc_get_numanode_obj_by_os_index
functions.description: Returns the NUMA node object with the given OS index, or NULL if none. Useful to map nodeset bit indexes to NUMA node objects.
requirements: topology must be valid.
os_index is an OS NUMA node identifier present in the topology.

functions.name: hwloc_get_closest_objs
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC unsigned hwloc_get_closest_objs(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_obj_t src, hwloc_obj_t * __hwloc_restrict objs, unsigned max);
functions.description: Performs a depth-first traversal to find and sort objects at the same depth as src by physical proximity to src. Fills up to max entries in objs and returns the number filled. Returns 0 if src is an I/O object.
requirements: topology must be valid.
src must be an object with a CPU set (not an I/O object) for non-zero results.
objs must point to an array with capacity at least max.

functions.name: hwloc_get_obj_below_by_type
functions.signature: static __hwloc_inline hwloc_obj_t hwloc_get_obj_below_by_type(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_obj_type_t type1, unsigned idx1, hwloc_obj_type_t type2, unsigned idx2) __hwloc_attribute_pure;
functions.description: Finds the idx2-th object of type2 under the idx1-th object of type1, starting from the root. Indexes are within the parent, not global.
requirements: topology must be valid.
The involved objects (root, the type1 object, and the searched type2 object) must have CPU sets.
idx1 and idx2 are zero-based within their respective parents.

functions.name: hwloc_get_obj_below_array_by_type
functions.signature: static __hwloc_inline hwloc_obj_t hwloc_get_obj_below_array_by_type(hwloc_topology_t topology, int nr, hwloc_obj_type_t *typev, unsigned *idxv) __hwloc_attribute_pure;
functions.description: Walks a chain of nr (type, index) pairs from the root to find a descendant object. Indexes are within the current parent at each step. Returns NULL if any step fails.
requirements: topology must be valid.
nr must be non-negative; typev and idxv must point to arrays of length nr.
Root, intermediate, and target objects must have CPU sets.

functions.name: hwloc_get_obj_with_same_locality
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC hwloc_obj_t hwloc_get_obj_with_same_locality(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_obj_t src, hwloc_obj_type_t type, const char *subtype, const char *nameprefix, unsigned long flags);
functions.description: Finds an object of the requested type that has the same locality as src (same CPU/nodeset for normal/memory types; for PCI/OS devices, may return the parent PCI device or another OS device in the same PCI parent). Optionally filter by subtype and/or name prefix. Does not cross PCI bridges. Returns NULL if incompatible or no match.
requirements: topology must be valid.
src must be a valid object.
type must be compatible with src's kind (no conversion between CPU/memory and I/O/Misc).
subtype may be NULL or a case-insensitive string to match the object's subtype attribute.
nameprefix may be NULL or a case-insensitive prefix of the object's name.
flags must be 0.

functions.name: hwloc_distrib
functions.signature: static __hwloc_inline int hwloc_distrib(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_obj_t *roots, unsigned n_roots, hwloc_cpuset_t *set, unsigned n, int until, unsigned long flags);
functions.description: Recursively distributes n items as CPU sets across the topology under the given root objects, proportionally to cpuset weights, stopping at depth 'until' (or INT_MAX to reach finest level). Optionally distributes in reverse order. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error (errno=EINVAL) if n is 0 or flags contain unsupported bits.
requirements: topology must be valid.
roots must point to an array of n_roots objects; if a root is memory/I/O/Misc, it is promoted to its nearest normal parent.
Each roots[i] must (ultimately) have a non-empty cpuset to receive weight; roots with zero weight are skipped.
set must point to an array of at least n hwloc_cpuset_t outputs; elements will be assigned (duplicated or recursively distributed).
n must be > 0.
until is a depth threshold; distribution stops if root has no children, chunk <= 1, or root->depth >= until.
flags must be 0 or include only HWLOC_DISTRIB_FLAG_REVERSE.
Caller should consider calling hwloc_bitmap_singlify() on resulting sets before binding to avoid migration.
On hybrid/asymmetric platforms, distribution can be suboptimal; prefer distributing within homogeneous domains.

functions.name: hwloc_topology_get_complete_cpuset
functions.description: Returns the complete CPU set of processors of the system. Equivalent to the root object's complete cpuset. The returned bitmap is not owned by the caller.
requirements: topology must be valid.
Do not modify or free the returned cpuset; duplicate it with hwloc_bitmap_dup() if a local copy is needed.

functions.name: hwloc_topology_get_topology_cpuset
functions.description: Returns the CPU set for which hwloc provides topology information (root object cpuset). The returned bitmap is not owned by the caller.
requirements: topology must be valid.
Do not modify or free the returned cpuset; duplicate it with hwloc_bitmap_dup() for a local copy.

functions.name: hwloc_topology_get_allowed_cpuset
functions.description: Returns the set of allowed CPUs. If the topology flag INCLUDE_DISALLOWED is not set, this equals the topology cpuset. The returned bitmap is not owned by the caller.
requirements: topology must be valid.
Do not modify or free the returned cpuset; duplicate it with hwloc_bitmap_dup() for a local copy.
If INCLUDE_DISALLOWED is set, use hwloc_bitmap_intersects()/and() with object cpusets to filter allowed PUs.

functions.name: hwloc_topology_get_complete_nodeset
functions.description: Returns the complete nodeset of the system (root object's complete nodeset). The returned bitmap is not owned by the caller.
requirements: topology must be valid.
Do not modify or free the returned nodeset; duplicate it with hwloc_bitmap_dup() for a local copy.

functions.name: hwloc_topology_get_topology_nodeset
functions.description: Returns the nodeset for which hwloc provides topology information (root object's nodeset). The returned bitmap is not owned by the caller.
requirements: topology must be valid.
Do not modify or free the returned nodeset; duplicate it with hwloc_bitmap_dup() for a local copy.

functions.name: hwloc_topology_get_allowed_nodeset
functions.description: Returns the set of allowed NUMA nodes. If INCLUDE_DISALLOWED is not set, this equals the topology nodeset. The returned bitmap is not owned by the caller.
requirements: topology must be valid.
Do not modify or free the returned nodeset; duplicate it with hwloc_bitmap_dup() for a local copy.
If INCLUDE_DISALLOWED is set, use hwloc_bitmap_intersects()/and() with object nodesets to filter allowed nodes.

functions.name: hwloc_cpuset_to_nodeset
functions.signature: static __hwloc_inline int hwloc_cpuset_to_nodeset(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_const_cpuset_t _cpuset, hwloc_nodeset_t nodeset);
functions.description: Converts a CPU set to the set of local NUMA nodes by setting nodes that are local to any PU in the cpuset. Nodes with no CPUs are never set. Returns 0 on success, -1 with errno=ENOMEM on internal allocation failure.
requirements: topology must be valid and must contain NUMA nodes (depth for HWLOC_OBJ_NUMANODE must not be UNKNOWN; asserted in code).
_cpuset must be a valid cpuset.
nodeset must be a valid, mutable nodeset bitmap.

functions.name: hwloc_cpuset_from_nodeset
functions.signature: static __hwloc_inline int hwloc_cpuset_from_nodeset(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_cpuset_t _cpuset, hwloc_const_nodeset_t nodeset);
functions.description: Converts a NUMA nodeset into a CPU set by OR-ing cpusets of NUMA nodes whose OS index is set in nodeset. CPUs with no local NUMA nodes are never set. Returns 0 on success, -1 with errno=ENOMEM on internal allocation failure.
requirements: topology must be valid and provide NUMA node depth (asserted).
_cpuset must be a valid, mutable cpuset bitmap.
nodeset must be a valid nodeset.

functions.name: hwloc_get_non_io_ancestor_obj
functions.description: Given an I/O object, returns the nearest ancestor that is not an I/O object (i.e., has non-NULL CPU/node sets). Typically usable for binding. Never returns NULL per documentation.
requirements: ioobj must be a valid object; typically an I/O object. Function walks up until finding cpuset != NULL.

functions.name: hwloc_get_next_pcidev
functions.signature: static __hwloc_inline hwloc_obj_t hwloc_get_next_pcidev(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_obj_t prev);
functions.description: Iterates over PCI device objects. Pass NULL prev for the first PCI device; otherwise pass the previous PCI device.
requirements: topology must be valid.
prev must be NULL or a previously returned PCI device from the same topology.

functions.name: hwloc_get_pcidev_by_busid
functions.signature: static __hwloc_inline hwloc_obj_t hwloc_get_pcidev_by_busid(hwloc_topology_t topology, unsigned domain, unsigned bus, unsigned dev, unsigned func);
functions.description: Finds a PCI device object matching the given PCI domain:bus:device.function identifiers. Returns NULL if none.
requirements: topology must be valid.
domain, bus, dev, func must match an existing PCI device in the topology.

functions.name: hwloc_get_pcidev_by_busidstring
functions.description: Parses a PCI bus ID string (formats: "yy:zz.t" or "xxxx:yy:zz.t") and returns the matching PCI device, or NULL. On parse failure, sets errno=EINVAL and returns NULL.
requirements: topology must be valid.
busid must be a non-NULL C string in one of the supported formats.
On invalid format, caller should check for NULL and may inspect errno (EINVAL).

functions.name: hwloc_get_next_osdev
functions.signature: static __hwloc_inline hwloc_obj_t hwloc_get_next_osdev(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_obj_t prev);
functions.description: Iterates over OS device objects. Pass NULL prev for the first OS device; otherwise pass the previous one.
requirements: topology must be valid.
prev must be NULL or a previously returned OS device from the same topology.

functions.name: hwloc_get_next_bridge
functions.signature: static __hwloc_inline hwloc_obj_t hwloc_get_next_bridge(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_obj_t prev);
functions.description: Iterates over bridge objects. Pass NULL prev for the first bridge; otherwise pass the previous one.
requirements: topology must be valid.
prev must be NULL or a previously returned bridge from the same topology.

functions.name: hwloc_bridge_covers_pcibus
functions.signature: static __hwloc_inline int hwloc_bridge_covers_pcibus(hwloc_obj_t bridge, unsigned domain, unsigned bus);
functions.description: Returns 1 if the given bridge is a PCI bridge covering the specified (domain,bus) according to its downstream secondary/subordinate bus range, 0 otherwise.
requirements: bridge must be a valid object; the function checks bridge->type == HWLOC_OBJ_BRIDGE and downstream_type == HWLOC_OBJ_BRIDGE_PCI.

functions.name: hwloc_distances_get
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_distances_get(hwloc_topology_t topology, unsigned *nr, struct hwloc_distances_s **distances, unsigned long kind, unsigned long flags);
functions.description: Retrieve distance matrices from a topology, optionally filtered by kind. On input, *nr is the capacity of the distances array; on output, *nr is the total number found (which may exceed the capacity). Each returned matrix must later be released with hwloc_distances_release(). Pointers objs and values inside each returned structure must not be replaced or freed; callers may modify kind and the contents of objs/values. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.
requirements: topology must be a valid, initialized hwloc topology
nr must be non-NULL and point to the input capacity; it is overwritten with the number found
distances must be either NULL (to only query the count) or point to an array with capacity of at least the input *nr
kind may be 0 (no filter) or an OR of HWLOC_DISTANCES_KIND_FROM_* and/or HWLOC_DISTANCES_KIND_VALUE_* filters
flags must be 0
Each returned distances structure must be released with hwloc_distances_release() unless removed with hwloc_distances_release_remove()
Callers must not replace, reallocate, or free distances->objs or distances->values pointers; they may modify distances->kind and the contents of distances->objs/values

functions.name: hwloc_distances_get_by_depth
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_distances_get_by_depth(hwloc_topology_t topology, int depth, unsigned *nr, struct hwloc_distances_s **distances, unsigned long kind, unsigned long flags);
functions.description: Retrieve distance matrices for objects at a specific topology depth, with the same semantics as hwloc_distances_get() and an added depth filter. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.
requirements: topology must be valid/initialized
depth must specify a valid depth in the topology
nr must be non-NULL and used as capacity input/output as in hwloc_distances_get()
distances must be NULL or point to an array with capacity of at least the input *nr
kind may be 0 or an OR of HWLOC_DISTANCES_KIND_FROM_* and/or HWLOC_DISTANCES_KIND_VALUE_* filters
flags must be 0
Each returned distances structure must be released with hwloc_distances_release() unless removed with hwloc_distances_release_remove()
Do not replace/reallocate/free distances->objs or distances->values; contents may be modified

functions.name: hwloc_distances_get_by_type
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_distances_get_by_type(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_obj_type_t type, unsigned *nr, struct hwloc_distances_s **distances, unsigned long kind, unsigned long flags);
functions.description: Retrieve distance matrices for objects of a specific type, otherwise identical to hwloc_distances_get(). Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.
requirements: topology must be valid/initialized
type must correspond to a valid object type present in the topology
nr must be non-NULL and used as capacity input/output as in hwloc_distances_get()
distances must be NULL or point to an array with capacity of at least the input *nr
kind may be 0 or an OR of HWLOC_DISTANCES_KIND_FROM_* and/or HWLOC_DISTANCES_KIND_VALUE_* filters
flags must be 0
Each returned distances structure must be released with hwloc_distances_release() unless removed with hwloc_distances_release_remove()
Do not replace/reallocate/free distances->objs or distances->values; contents may be modified

functions.name: hwloc_distances_get_by_name
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_distances_get_by_name(hwloc_topology_t topology, const char *name, unsigned *nr, struct hwloc_distances_s **distances, unsigned long flags);
functions.description: Retrieve distance matrices that match a given name (for example, "NUMALatency", "XGMIBandwidth"). Usually only one structure matches a given name. Same storage/count semantics as hwloc_distances_get(). Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.
requirements: topology must be valid/initialized
name may be any constant string identifying the distance structure
nr must be non-NULL and used as capacity input/output as in hwloc_distances_get()
distances must be NULL or point to an array with capacity of at least the input *nr
flags must be 0
Each returned distances structure must be released with hwloc_distances_release() unless removed with hwloc_distances_release_remove()
Do not replace/reallocate/free distances->objs or distances->values; contents may be modified

functions.name: hwloc_distances_get_name
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC const char * hwloc_distances_get_name(hwloc_topology_t topology, struct hwloc_distances_s *distances);
functions.description: Return a constant descriptive name for a distances structure (e.g., "NUMALatency"), or NULL if unknown. The returned string belongs to the library and must not be freed.
requirements: topology must be valid/initialized
distances must be a structure previously obtained (and not yet released) from hwloc_distances_get() or variants
Caller must not free or modify the returned string

functions.name: hwloc_distances_release
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC void hwloc_distances_release(hwloc_topology_t topology, struct hwloc_distances_s *distances);
functions.description: Release a distances structure previously returned by hwloc_distances_get() or its variants. Not required if the structure is removed via hwloc_distances_release_remove().
requirements: topology must be valid/initialized
distances must be a structure previously returned by hwloc_distances_get() or variants and not already released/removed
Do not use the distances pointer after release

functions.name: hwloc_distances_transform
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_distances_transform(hwloc_topology_t topology, struct hwloc_distances_s *distances, enum hwloc_distances_transform_e transform, void *transform_attr, unsigned long flags);
functions.description: Apply a transformation (e.g., remove NULL objects, convert bandwidths to link counts, merge switch ports, or compute a transitive closure) to a distances structure previously obtained with hwloc_distances_get() or variants. Modifies the local copy only; to persist in topology, add a new structure and remove the old via hwloc_distances_release_remove(). Returns 0 on success, -1 on error (e.g., invalid flags or invalid transformation semantics).
requirements: topology must be valid/initialized
distances must be a valid structure obtained from hwloc_distances_get() or variants
transform must be one of enum hwloc_distances_transform_e values
transform_attr must be NULL for now
flags must be 0
Callers must tolerate that distances->objs and distances->values contents may be modified
When using HWLOC_DISTANCES_TRANSFORM_REMOVE_NULL, at least 2 objects must remain; otherwise the function returns -1 with errno set to EINVAL

functions.name: hwloc_distances_obj_index
functions.signature: static __hwloc_inline int hwloc_distances_obj_index(struct hwloc_distances_s *distances, hwloc_obj_t obj);
functions.description: Return the index of obj in distances->objs, or -1 if the object is not present. Convenience inline helper for scanning matrices.
requirements: distances must be non-NULL and point to a valid distances structure
obj may be any hwloc object; must be exactly equal to one in distances->objs to be found

functions.name: hwloc_distances_obj_pair_values
functions.signature: static __hwloc_inline int hwloc_distances_obj_pair_values(struct hwloc_distances_s *distances, hwloc_obj_t obj1, hwloc_obj_t obj2, hwloc_uint64_t *value1to2, hwloc_uint64_t *value2to1);
functions.description: Fetch the two directed distance values between obj1 and obj2 from a distances matrix. Stores obj1->obj2 in value1to2 and obj2->obj1 in value2to1. Returns 0 on success, -1 if either object is not present.
requirements: distances must be non-NULL and valid
obj1 and obj2 must both be present in distances->objs
value1to2 and value2to1 must be non-NULL pointers to writable hwloc_uint64_t storage

functions.name: hwloc_distances_add_create
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC hwloc_distances_add_handle_t hwloc_distances_add_create(hwloc_topology_t topology, const char *name, unsigned long kind, unsigned long flags);
functions.description: Create an empty distances structure to be populated with objects and values via hwloc_distances_add_values() and then finalized with hwloc_distances_add_commit(). Parameter name is optional (may be NULL). Returns a handle on success, NULL on error.
requirements: topology must be valid/initialized and open for modification
name may be NULL or a string; if non-NULL it is copied and may be freed by the caller afterward

kind must be an OR’ed set of hwloc_distances_kind_e with at most one FROM_* and exactly one VALUE_* meaning (as appropriate); HETEROGENEOUS_TYPES will be set automatically during values addition if needed
flags must be 0
The returned handle must be passed to hwloc_distances_add_values() and then to hwloc_distances_add_commit(), or it is discarded implicitly on error

functions.name: hwloc_distances_add_values
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_distances_add_values(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_distances_add_handle_t handle, unsigned nbobjs, hwloc_obj_t *objs, hwloc_uint64_t *values, unsigned long flags);
functions.description: Attach the set of objects and their pairwise distance matrix to a distances structure created by hwloc_distances_add_create().
