Arrays are copied internally. nbobjs must be at least 2. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error (in which case the temporary structure and its contents are destroyed).
requirements: topology must be valid/initialized and open for modification
handle must be a valid handle previously returned by hwloc_distances_add_create() and not yet committed
nbobjs must be at least 2
objs must point to an array of nbobjs valid objects
values must point to an array of nbobjs*nbobjs entries laid out with entry i*nbobjs + j for distance i->j
flags must be 0
Caller may free objs and values after this call since they are copied internally

functions.name: hwloc_distances_add_commit
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_distances_add_commit(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_distances_add_handle_t handle, unsigned long flags);
functions.description: Finalize and insert the new distances structure into the topology. Optionally request grouping via flags. On error, the temporary structure and its contents are destroyed. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.
requirements: topology must be valid/initialized and open for modification
handle must be a valid uncommitted handle previously used with hwloc_distances_add_values()
flags may be 0 or an OR of hwloc_distances_add_flag_e values (HWLOC_DISTANCES_ADD_FLAG_GROUP and/or HWLOC_DISTANCES_ADD_FLAG_GROUP_INACCURATE)

functions.name: hwloc_distances_remove
functions.description: Remove all distance matrices from a topology, regardless of provenance. If distances were used to group objects, those Group objects remain. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.
requirements: topology must be valid/initialized and open for modification

functions.name: hwloc_distances_remove_by_depth
functions.description: Remove distance matrices only for objects at a specific topology depth. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.
requirements: topology must be valid/initialized and open for modification
depth must refer to a valid depth in the topology

functions.name: hwloc_distances_remove_by_type
functions.description: Helper that removes distance matrices for a specific object type by mapping type to a unique depth and calling hwloc_distances_remove_by_depth(). If the type maps to an unknown or multiple depths, it returns 0 without removing anything.
requirements: topology must be valid/initialized and open for modification
type should map to a unique depth via hwloc_get_type_depth(); if it is HWLOC_TYPE_DEPTH_UNKNOWN or HWLOC_TYPE_DEPTH_MULTIPLE, nothing is removed and the function returns 0

functions.name: hwloc_distances_release_remove
functions.description: Release and remove a specific distances structure from the topology. This includes a call to hwloc_distances_release(). Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.
requirements: topology must be valid/initialized and open for modification
distances must be a distances structure currently present in the topology and not already released/removed
Do not use the distances pointer after successful removal

functions.name: hwloc_topology_diff_build
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_topology_diff_build(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_topology_t newtopology, unsigned long flags, hwloc_topology_diff_t *diff);
functions.description: Compute a list of differences between two hwloc topologies. The result is a linked list of diff elements stored via the output parameter diff. Returns 0 if the diff is fully representable (diff may be set to NULL if there is no difference), 1 if parts are too complex to represent (TOO_COMPLEX entries are queued), or -1 on error. Intended for compressing similar topologies and later applying or exporting simple attribute changes.
requirements: topology must be a valid, initialized hwloc_topology_t.
newtopology must be a valid, initialized hwloc_topology_t.
flags is currently not used and should be 0.
diff must be a valid pointer to receive the head of the diff list; on success, the caller must later free the list with hwloc_topology_diff_destroy().
Only simple attribute differences are supported; complex structural differences cause return value 1 and insertion of HWLOC_TOPOLOGY_DIFF_TOO_COMPLEX entries.
A diff that contains HWLOC_TOPOLOGY_DIFF_TOO_COMPLEX entries cannot be exported to XML nor applied with hwloc_topology_diff_apply().
The output diff list may be edited by removing entries; any removed entries must be destroyed with hwloc_topology_diff_destroy() (as a list).

functions.name: hwloc_topology_diff_apply
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_topology_diff_apply(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_topology_diff_t diff, unsigned long flags);
functions.description: Apply a previously built topology diff to an existing topology (modifying it in place). Supports reverse application via HWLOC_TOPOLOGY_DIFF_APPLY_REVERSE in flags. If the application fails part‑way, all changes already applied are rolled back before returning. Returns 0 on success, or a negative value -N indicating failure while applying the N-th element.
requirements: topology must be a valid, initialized hwloc_topology_t; it will be modified in place (duplicate first with hwloc_topology_dup() if needed).
diff must be a valid diff list produced by hwloc_topology_diff_build() that contains no HWLOC_TOPOLOGY_DIFF_TOO_COMPLEX entries.
flags must be an OR'ed set of hwloc_topology_diff_apply_flags_e values (0 or HWLOC_TOPOLOGY_DIFF_APPLY_REVERSE).
Caller must handle negative return values, where -N indicates which diff element failed to apply.

functions.name: hwloc_topology_diff_destroy
functions.description: Destroy (free) a list of topology differences previously created (e.g., by hwloc_topology_diff_build or by removing entries from an existing list). Always returns 0.
requirements: diff must be a valid diff list to destroy (as produced by hwloc_topology_diff_build() or by splitting/removing entries from such a list).
All entries removed from a diff list by the caller should be passed (as a list) to this function to avoid leaks.

functions.name: hwloc_topology_diff_load_xml
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_topology_diff_load_xml(const char *xmlpath, hwloc_topology_diff_t *diff, char **refname);
functions.description: Load a topology diff list from an XML file located at xmlpath. On success, stores the head of the diff list in diff and, if refname is not NULL and the file specifies it, returns an identifier for the reference topology used when the diff was computed. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.
requirements: xmlpath must point to a readable XML file containing a topology diff.
diff must be a valid pointer to receive the resulting diff list; the caller must later destroy it with hwloc_topology_diff_destroy().
If refname is not NULL and the XML contains a reference identifier, the function sets *refname to a newly allocated string that the caller must free.
Caller should only attempt to apply or re-export diffs that do not contain HWLOC_TOPOLOGY_DIFF_TOO_COMPLEX entries.

functions.name: hwloc_topology_diff_export_xml
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_topology_diff_export_xml(hwloc_topology_diff_t diff, const char *refname, const char *xmlpath);
functions.description: Export a topology diff list to an XML file at xmlpath. Optionally includes refname as the identifier of the reference topology used when computing the diff. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.
requirements: diff must be a valid diff list that contains no HWLOC_TOPOLOGY_DIFF_TOO_COMPLEX entries.
xmlpath must specify a writable path where the XML file will be created/overwritten.
refname may be NULL or a valid C string to embed as the reference identifier.

functions.name: hwloc_topology_diff_load_xmlbuffer
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_topology_diff_load_xmlbuffer(const char *xmlbuffer, int buflen, hwloc_topology_diff_t *diff, char **refname);
functions.description: Load a topology diff list from an in-memory XML buffer. The buffer is given by xmlbuffer with length buflen (including the terminating '\0'). On success, stores the diff list in diff and, if refname is not NULL and present in the XML, returns the reference topology identifier string. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.
requirements: xmlbuffer must point to a buffer containing a NUL-terminated XML diff; buflen must include the ending '\0'.
buflen must be the size of the buffer including the terminating NUL.
diff must be a valid pointer to receive the resulting diff list; the caller must later destroy it with hwloc_topology_diff_destroy().
If refname is not NULL and the XML contains a reference identifier, the function sets *refname to a newly allocated string that the caller must free.

functions.name: hwloc_topology_diff_export_xmlbuffer
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_topology_diff_export_xmlbuffer(hwloc_topology_diff_t diff, const char *refname, char **xmlbuffer, int *buflen);
functions.description: Export a topology diff list to an in-memory XML buffer. Optionally includes refname as the identifier for the reference topology. On success, returns the allocated XML buffer (ending with a '\0') and its length (including the terminator) via xmlbuffer and buflen. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.
requirements: diff must be a valid diff list that contains no HWLOC_TOPOLOGY_DIFF_TOO_COMPLEX entries.
xmlbuffer must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the allocated buffer; the caller must free it later with hwloc_free_xmlbuffer().
buflen must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the length of the returned buffer including the terminating '\0'.
refname may be NULL or a valid C string to embed as the reference identifier.

functions.name: hwloc_memattr_get_by_name
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_memattr_get_by_name(hwloc_topology_t topology, const char *name, hwloc_memattr_id_t *id);
functions.description: Look up a memory attribute by its string name and return its attribute ID. Use to translate a human-readable attribute name into an hwloc_memattr_id_t before querying values or flags.
requirements: topology must be a valid, initialized hwloc_topology_t
name must refer to an existing memory attribute (returns -1 and sets errno=EINVAL otherwise)
id must be a valid pointer to receive the resulting attribute ID (inferred from signature)

functions.name: hwloc_get_local_numanode_objs
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_get_local_numanode_objs(hwloc_topology_t topology, struct hwloc_location *location, unsigned *nr, hwloc_obj_t *nodes, unsigned long flags);
functions.description: Return an array of NUMA node objects whose locality matches or relates to the given location (cpuset or object), optionally extended by flags (larger/smaller/intersect/all). Useful to enumerate NUMA nodes near a set of CPUs or an object.
requirements: topology must be a valid, initialized hwloc_topology_t

location must be non-NULL and describe either a cpuset (type=HWLOC_LOCATION_TYPE_CPUSET) or an object (type=HWLOC_LOCATION_TYPE_OBJECT); if an object lacks a cpuset (e.g., I/O), its CPU parent is used
nr must be non-NULL and on input contain the capacity of the nodes array; on output it is set to the number of nodes found (may exceed input capacity)
nodes must point to an array of at least *nr input entries to receive up to that many hwloc_obj_t results
flags is a OR’ed set of hwloc_local_numanode_flag_e; may be 0 for exact-locality selection
Returned node objects belong to the topology and must not be modified or freed
Function returns 0 on success, -1 on error

functions.name: hwloc_topology_get_default_nodeset
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_topology_get_default_nodeset(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_nodeset_t nodeset, unsigned long flags);
functions.description: Fill nodeset with the set of NUMA nodes considered default for regular allocations (typically DRAM) on heterogeneous-memory machines. Often used to restrict a topology to default nodes or to enumerate NUMA domains for task placement.
requirements: topology must be a valid, initialized hwloc_topology_t
nodeset must be a valid hwloc_nodeset_t to receive the result
flags must be 0
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error
Returned nodeset is included in the topology’s available nodes; may be strictly smaller on heterogeneous systems

functions.name: hwloc_memattr_get_value
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_memattr_get_value(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_memattr_id_t attribute, hwloc_obj_t target_node, struct hwloc_location *initiator, unsigned long flags, hwloc_uint64_t *value);
functions.description: Query the numeric value of a memory attribute for a given target NUMA node, optionally as seen from a specific initiator (cpuset or object). Attributes such as Bandwidth/Latency may depend on the initiator; others (Capacity/Locality) do not.
requirements: topology must be a valid, initialized hwloc_topology_t
attribute must exist; otherwise returns -1 (errno=EINVAL)
target_node must be non-NULL
If attribute is HWLOC_MEMATTR_ID_CAPACITY, target_node must be a NUMA node
If attribute is HWLOC_MEMATTR_ID_LOCALITY, target_node must have a CPU set
If the attribute lacks HWLOC_MEMATTR_FLAG_NEED_INITIATOR, initiator is ignored and may be NULL
flags must be 0
value must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the attribute value (inferred from signature)
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error

functions.name: hwloc_memattr_get_best_target
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_memattr_get_best_target(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_memattr_id_t attribute, struct hwloc_location *initiator, unsigned long flags, hwloc_obj_t *best_target, hwloc_uint64_t *value);
functions.description: Select the best target NUMA node for a given memory attribute, optionally relative to an initiator when the attribute depends on it. Optionally returns the attribute value for that best target. Use when picking where to allocate memory (e.g., lowest latency or highest bandwidth).
requirements: topology must be a valid, initialized hwloc_topology_t
attribute must exist; otherwise returns -1 (errno=EINVAL)
If the attribute lacks HWLOC_MEMATTR_FLAG_NEED_INITIATOR, initiator is ignored and may be NULL
flags must be 0
best_target must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the chosen NUMA node (inferred from signature)
value may be NULL; if non-NULL, receives the attribute value for best_target
Returns 0 on success
Returns -1 with errno=ENOENT if there are no matching targets
Returns -1 with errno=EINVAL if flags are invalid or the attribute does not exist
Returned best_target belongs to the topology and must not be modified or freed

functions.name: hwloc_memattr_get_best_initiator
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_memattr_get_best_initiator(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_memattr_id_t attribute, hwloc_obj_t target_node, unsigned long flags, struct hwloc_location *best_initiator, hwloc_uint64_t *value);
functions.description: For a given target NUMA node and attribute that depends on an initiator, return one initiator that yields the best attribute value for that target. Optionally returns the value. Useful to find which CPUs/objects should access a memory node for best performance.
requirements: topology must be a valid, initialized hwloc_topology_t
target_node must be non-NULL
attribute must relate to a specific initiator (have HWLOC_MEMATTR_FLAG_NEED_INITIATOR); otherwise returns -1 (errno=EINVAL)
flags must be 0
best_initiator must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the result (inferred from signature)
value may be NULL; if non-NULL, receives the attribute value for best_initiator
Returns 0 on success
Returns -1 with errno=ENOENT if no matching initiators exist
Returned best_initiator refers to topology-owned data and must not be modified or freed

functions.name: hwloc_memattr_get_targets
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_memattr_get_targets(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_memattr_id_t attribute, struct hwloc_location *initiator, unsigned long flags, unsigned *nr, hwloc_obj_t *targets, hwloc_uint64_t *values);
functions.description: Enumerate target NUMA nodes that have a value for the given attribute (optionally for a given initiator when required). Optionally also return the corresponding attribute values. Intended mainly for tools/debugging or for applications that want to manually compare targets.
requirements: topology must be a valid, initialized hwloc_topology_t

attribute must exist; if the attribute lacks HWLOC_MEMATTR_FLAG_NEED_INITIATOR, initiator is ignored and may be NULL; otherwise initiator may be non-NULL to filter targets that have a value for that initiator
flags must be 0
nr must be non-NULL; on input, *nr is the capacity of the targets (and values) arrays; on output, *nr is the total number of targets found (may exceed input capacity)
targets must point to an array of at least the input *nr entries to receive up to that many topology-owned hwloc_obj_t (inferred from signature and description)
values may be NULL; if non-NULL, must point to an array of at least the input *nr entries to receive values
Returned targets belong to the topology and must not be modified or freed
Returns 0 on success or -1 on error

functions.name: hwloc_memattr_get_initiators
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_memattr_get_initiators(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_memattr_id_t attribute, hwloc_obj_t target_node, unsigned long flags, unsigned *nr, struct hwloc_location *initiators, hwloc_uint64_t *values);
functions.description: Enumerate initiators that have values for a given attribute with respect to a specific target NUMA node. Optionally also return the corresponding attribute values. Intended mainly for tools/debugging or advanced selection logic.
requirements: topology must be a valid, initialized hwloc_topology_t
target_node must be non-NULL
flags must be 0
If the attribute does not have HWLOC_MEMATTR_FLAG_NEED_INITIATOR, no initiator is returned
nr must be non-NULL; on input, *nr is the capacity of the initiators (and values) arrays; on output, *nr is the total number of initiators found (may exceed input capacity)
initiators must point to an array of at least the input *nr entries to receive up to that many struct hwloc_location results (inferred from signature and description)
values may be NULL; if non-NULL, must point to an array of at least the input *nr entries to receive values
Returned initiators belong to the topology and must not be modified or freed
Returns 0 on success or -1 on error

functions.name: hwloc_memattr_get_name
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_memattr_get_name(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_memattr_id_t attribute, const char **name);
functions.description: Retrieve the human-readable name of a memory attribute given its ID. Use when iterating over or displaying attributes.
requirements: topology must be a valid, initialized hwloc_topology_t
attribute must exist; otherwise returns -1 with errno=EINVAL
name must be a non-NULL output pointer (explicitly required)
Returns 0 on success

functions.name: hwloc_memattr_get_flags
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_memattr_get_flags(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_memattr_id_t attribute, unsigned long *flags);
functions.description: Retrieve the flag set of a memory attribute, indicating preference direction (higher/lower is better) and whether an initiator is required.
requirements: topology must be a valid, initialized hwloc_topology_t
attribute must exist; otherwise returns -1 with errno=EINVAL
flags must be a non-NULL output pointer (explicitly required)
Returns 0 on success

functions.name: hwloc_memattr_register
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_memattr_register(hwloc_topology_t topology, const char *name, unsigned long flags, hwloc_memattr_id_t *id);
functions.description: Register a new custom memory attribute with the given name and flags, returning its newly assigned ID (immediately after the last existing attribute). Use to extend hwloc with application- or platform-specific attributes.
requirements: topology must be a valid, initialized hwloc_topology_t
name must be unique; returns -1 with errno=EBUSY if another attribute already uses this name
flags must include exactly one of HWLOC_MEMATTR_FLAG_HIGHER_FIRST or HWLOC_MEMATTR_FLAG_LOWER_FIRST, but not both; returns -1 with errno=EINVAL otherwise
id must be a valid pointer to receive the new attribute ID (inferred from signature)
Returns 0 on success

functions.name: hwloc_memattr_set_value
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_memattr_set_value(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_memattr_id_t attribute, hwloc_obj_t target_node, struct hwloc_location *initiator, unsigned long flags, hwloc_uint64_t value);
functions.description: Set or update the value of a memory attribute for a specific target NUMA node, optionally for a specific initiator if the attribute requires it. The initiator location is copied internally; the caller retains ownership of any allocated resources used to describe it.
requirements: topology must be a valid, initialized hwloc_topology_t
attribute must not be HWLOC_MEMATTR_ID_CAPACITY or HWLOC_MEMATTR_ID_LOCALITY (these cannot be modified)
target_node must be non-NULL
If the attribute does not have HWLOC_MEMATTR_FLAG_NEED_INITIATOR, initiator is ignored and may be NULL
If providing an initiator, it should be of type HWLOC_LOCATION_TYPE_CPUSET when referring to CPU core accesses (note: object type is currently unused internally)
The initiator is copied into the topology; the caller should free anything allocated to store the initiator (e.g., the cpuset)
flags must be 0
Returns 0 on success or -1 on error

functions.name: hwloc_cpukinds_get_nr
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_cpukinds_get_nr(hwloc_topology_t topology, unsigned long flags);
functions.description: Returns the number of CPU kinds detected in the given topology. Use when you need to iterate over or query per-kind information. If the platform is homogeneous but exposes kinds, this may be 1; if no kind information is available, returns 0. Flags are currently unused and must be 0.
requirements: topology must be a valid, initialized, and loaded hwloc_topology_t
flags must be 0
callers must check the return value: >=1 is success with kinds, 0 means no kind information, -1 indicates error with errno set to EINVAL for invalid flags

functions.name: hwloc_cpukinds_get_by_cpuset
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_cpukinds_get_by_cpuset(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_const_bitmap_t cpuset, unsigned long flags);
functions.description: Returns the index of the CPU kind that fully contains all PUs in the given cpuset. Use to map a set of PUs to its corresponding kind. If the cpuset only partially overlaps a kind, returns -1 with errno=EXDEV; if it doesn’t overlap any kind at all, returns -1 with errno=ENOENT.
requirements: topology must be a valid, initialized, and loaded hwloc_topology_t
cpuset must be a non-NULL hwloc bitmap referencing PUs from the topology
flags must be 0

callers must handle error returns: -1 with errno=EXDEV if cpuset is only partially included in some kind; -1 with errno=ENOENT if not included in any kind; -1 with errno=EINVAL if parameters are invalid

functions.name: hwloc_cpukinds_get_info
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_cpukinds_get_info(hwloc_topology_t topology, unsigned kind_index, hwloc_bitmap_t cpuset, int *efficiency, struct hwloc_infos_s **infosp, unsigned long flags);
functions.description: Retrieves details about a specific CPU kind, including its PU set (optionally into cpuset), its relative efficiency rank (optionally into efficiency), and an array of info attributes (optionally via infosp). Use after obtaining the number of kinds and selecting a kind index. Kinds with lower efficiency are reported first (0 is most energy-efficient). If efficiencies are unknown, all efficiencies are -1 and ordering is unspecified. The info array belongs to the library and must not be freed or modified.
requirements: topology must be a valid, initialized, and loaded hwloc_topology_t
kind_index must be between 0 and hwloc_cpukinds_get_nr(topology,0)-1
cpuset may be NULL; if non-NULL, it must be a valid hwloc bitmap to receive the PUs of the kind
efficiency may be NULL; if non-NULL, it must point to an int to receive the efficiency rank (0..nr_kinds-1, or -1 if unknown)
infosp may be NULL; if non-NULL, it receives a pointer to an internal info array that must not be freed or modified by the caller
flags must be 0
callers must check the return value: 0 on success; -1 with errno=ENOENT if kind_index is invalid; -1 with errno=EINVAL if parameters are invalid

functions.name: hwloc_cpukinds_register
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_cpukinds_register(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_bitmap_t cpuset, int forced_efficiency, struct hwloc_infos_s *infos, unsigned long flags);
functions.description: Registers a new CPU kind for the PUs in cpuset with optional info attributes and an optional forced efficiency. Used to annotate or refine kinds in the topology. If cpuset overlaps existing kinds, hwloc may split and/or merge information across kinds accordingly. The provided cpuset and infos are duplicated internally; the caller remains responsible for freeing the originals. The forced_efficiency can be -1 (unknown) or a value used to rank kinds, but hwloc will rescale efficiencies across all kinds to 0..(nr_kinds-1).
requirements: topology must be a valid, initialized, and loaded hwloc_topology_t
cpuset must be non-NULL and non-empty; otherwise the function fails with errno=EINVAL
forced_efficiency must be -1 for unknown or a valid integer efficiency hint (values are later rescaled by hwloc)
infos may be NULL or point to an array of info attributes; the array is duplicated internally, and the caller must free its own copy
flags must be 0
callers must check the return value: 0 on success; -1 with errno=EINVAL if parameters are invalid (e.g., NULL or empty cpuset)

functions.name: hwloc_shmem_topology_get_length
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_shmem_topology_get_length(hwloc_topology_t topology, size_t *lengthp, unsigned long flags);
functions.description: Get the required shared-memory buffer size (in bytes) needed to duplicate the given hwloc topology into a file-backed shared-memory region for inter-process sharing. Typical usage: call this first to obtain the length to use with hwloc_shmem_topology_write() and hwloc_shmem_topology_adopt(). Flags are currently unused and must be 0. Returns the length via lengthp and 0 on success, or -1 on error (e.g., invalid flags).
requirements: topology must be a valid hwloc_topology_t handle.
lengthp must be non-NULL and writable to receive the required length.
flags must be 0 (currently unused).
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; -1 indicates failure (e.g., invalid flags).

functions.name: hwloc_shmem_topology_write
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_shmem_topology_write(hwloc_topology_t topology, int fd, hwloc_uint64_t fileoffset, void *mmap_address, size_t length, unsigned long flags);
functions.description: Duplicate an existing hwloc topology into a file-backed shared-memory segment. The function temporarily maps the file region [fd + fileoffset, length] at the fixed virtual address mmap_address and places a duplicate of the topology there. The mapping length must have been obtained earlier with hwloc_shmem_topology_get_length() and the topology must not have changed since. The object userdata pointer is duplicated as a pointer, but any pointed buffer is not automatically shared. Returns 0 on success, or -1 on error with errno set (EBUSY if the requested mapping is unavailable; EINVAL if fileoffset, mmap_address, or length are not page-aligned). Flags are currently unused and must be 0.
requirements: topology must be a valid hwloc_topology_t handle and must not have been modified since the length was obtained via hwloc_shmem_topology_get_length().
length must match the value previously returned by hwloc_shmem_topology_get_length() for this topology.
fileoffset must be page-aligned.
mmap_address must be page-aligned and refer to a virtual memory region available for mapping; if unavailable, the call fails with errno=EBUSY.
length must be page-aligned.
fd must be an open file descriptor referring to the destination file to back the shared-memory region.
mmap_address and length should correspond to an address range that is available in all processes that will share the topology (to ensure identical virtual addresses).
flags must be 0 (currently unused).
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; -1 indicates failure and errno is set to indicate the cause (EBUSY or EINVAL as documented).
If sharing userdata buffers is desired, the caller must allocate and manage those buffers in shared memory separately; only the userdata pointer value is duplicated.

functions.name: hwloc_shmem_topology_adopt
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_shmem_topology_adopt(hwloc_topology_t *topologyp, int fd, hwloc_uint64_t fileoffset, void *mmap_address, size_t length, unsigned long flags);
functions.description: Adopt a topology stored in a file-backed shared-memory region previously created with hwloc_shmem_topology_write(). The function maps the file region [fd + fileoffset, length] at the fixed virtual address mmap_address and returns a read-only hwloc topology through topologyp. The adopted topology must be destroyed with hwloc_topology_destroy() when done. It is read-only: it cannot be modified (e.g., hwloc_topology_restrict() and userdata modifications are not allowed). hwloc_topology_allow() may be used to change allowed sets if the original topology was loaded with HWLOC_TOPOLOGY_FLAG_INCLUDE_DISALLOWED. Returns 0 on success, or -1 on error with errno set (EBUSY if the requested mapping is unavailable; EINVAL if page-alignment or parameters do not match the writer’s, or if topology layout/ABI differs). Flags are currently unused and must be 0.
requirements: topologyp must be non-NULL and writable; on success it receives the adopted topology handle.
fd, fileoffset, mmap_address, and length must be identical to those used with hwloc_shmem_topology_write() for the shared topology.
fileoffset must be page-aligned.
mmap_address must be page-aligned and the specified mapping must be available; if unavailable, the call fails with errno=EBUSY.
length must be page-aligned and must match the length used by the writer.
flags must be 0 (currently unused).
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; -1 indicates failure and errno is set (EBUSY, EINVAL for parameter mismatch or ABI/layout mismatch).
On success, the returned topology is read-only; do not call functions that modify topology structure (e.g., hwloc_topology_restrict()) or change object userdata pointers.
If hwloc_topology_allow() is to be used to change allowed sets, the original (writer) topology must have been loaded with HWLOC_TOPOLOGY_FLAG_INCLUDE_DISALLOWED.
The adopted topology must be released with hwloc_topology_destroy() when no longer needed.

functions.name: hwloc_bitmap_alloc
functions.description: Allocate and return a new empty hwloc bitmap. Returns NULL on allocation failure. Use hwloc_bitmap_free() to release the bitmap.
requirements: Caller must free the returned bitmap with hwloc_bitmap_free() when no longer needed.
Caller must check for NULL return to detect allocation failure.

functions.name: hwloc_bitmap_alloc_full
functions.description: Allocate and return a new full hwloc bitmap (all bits set, infinitely set). Returns NULL on allocation failure. Use hwloc_bitmap_free() to release the bitmap.
requirements: Caller must free the returned bitmap with hwloc_bitmap_free() when no longer needed.
Caller must check for NULL return to detect allocation failure.

functions.name: hwloc_bitmap_free
functions.description: Free a bitmap previously allocated by hwloc. No operation is performed if bitmap is NULL.
requirements: The bitmap argument must be either a valid hwloc_bitmap_t returned by an hwloc allocation function or NULL.
Do not use the bitmap after it has been freed.

functions.name: hwloc_bitmap_dup
functions.description: Duplicate a bitmap by allocating a new bitmap and copying the source contents. If the input bitmap is NULL, NULL is returned.
requirements: Caller must free the returned bitmap with hwloc_bitmap_free().
Caller must check for NULL return to detect allocation failure or NULL input.

functions.name: hwloc_bitmap_copy
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_bitmap_copy(hwloc_bitmap_t dst, hwloc_const_bitmap_t src);
functions.description: Copy the contents of bitmap src into the already-allocated bitmap dst. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error (e.g., internal reallocation failure).
requirements: dst must be a valid, already-allocated hwloc_bitmap_t.
src must be a valid hwloc_const_bitmap_t.
Caller should check for a -1 return to handle errors (e.g., ENOMEM).

functions.name: hwloc_bitmap_snprintf
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_bitmap_snprintf(char * __hwloc_restrict buf, size_t buflen, hwloc_const_bitmap_t bitmap);
functions.description: Format a bitmap into the default hwloc string format: a comma-separated list of hexadecimal 32-bit blocks (e.g., "0xffffffff,0x00000006,0x00000002"). Writes up to buflen chars into buf (buf may be NULL if buflen==0). Returns the number of characters written if not truncated, or the number that would have been written, excluding the terminating NUL, or -1 on error.
requirements: bitmap must be a valid bitmap.
If buflen is 0, buf may be NULL; otherwise buf must point to at least buflen bytes.
Caller must handle a return of -1 (error).
When displaying CPU or nodesets, note that they contain physical indexes (as documented).

functions.name: hwloc_bitmap_asprintf
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_bitmap_asprintf(char ** strp, hwloc_const_bitmap_t bitmap);
functions.description: Allocate and format a bitmap into a newly-allocated string in the default hwloc format (comma-separated hex 32-bit blocks). On success, *strp receives the allocated string; returns the number of characters written (excluding terminating NUL). Returns -1 on error (e.g., ENOMEM).
requirements: strp must be non-NULL and writable; on success, *strp must be freed by the caller (allocator not specified, but typical C free()).
bitmap must be a valid bitmap.
Caller must handle a return of -1 and that *strp is unspecified on error.
When displaying CPU or nodesets, note that they contain physical indexes.

functions.name: hwloc_bitmap_sscanf
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_bitmap_sscanf(hwloc_bitmap_t bitmap, const char * __hwloc_restrict string);
functions.description: Parse a bitmap from a string in the default hwloc format (comma-separated hexadecimal 32-bit blocks) and store it into bitmap. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.
requirements: bitmap must be a valid, writable bitmap.
string must be a valid NUL-terminated C string using the documented format (e.g., "0xffffffff,0x6,0x2").
Caller must handle a -1 return on invalid input or allocation failure.
If parsing CPU or nodesets, the input string must use physical indexes.

functions.name: hwloc_bitmap_list_snprintf
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_bitmap_list_snprintf(char * __hwloc_restrict buf, size_t buflen, hwloc_const_bitmap_t bitmap);
functions.description: Format a bitmap into a list string: comma-separated indexes or ranges (e.g., "1,33-34,64-95"; last range may be open-ended if infinitely set). Writes up to buflen chars (buf may be NULL if buflen==0). Returns number written if not truncated, or the number that would have been written (excluding NUL), or -1 on error.
requirements: bitmap must be valid.
If buflen is 0, buf may be NULL; otherwise buf must point to at least buflen bytes.
Caller must handle a return of -1 (error).
When displaying CPU or nodesets, note that they contain physical indexes.

functions.name: hwloc_bitmap_list_asprintf
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_bitmap_list_asprintf(char ** strp, hwloc_const_bitmap_t bitmap);
functions.description: Allocate and format a bitmap into a newly-allocated list string (e.g., "1,33-34,64-95"). Returns the number of characters written (excluding NUL), or -1 on error (e.g., ENOMEM).
requirements: strp must be non-NULL and writable; on success, *strp must be freed by the caller.
bitmap must be valid.
Caller must handle a return of -1 and unspecified *strp on error.

functions.description: Register an application-specific callback used during XML export to convert object userdata into exportable strings. The callback is invoked for each object with non-NULL userdata; it should call hwloc_export_obj_userdata() or hwloc_export_obj_userdata_base64() to emit data (possibly multiple times). Pass NULL to disable exporting userdata. The topology-specific userdata pointer is ignored for XML.
requirements: topology: must be a valid hwloc_topology_t handle.
export_cb may be NULL to disable exporting userdata.

Only printable characters may be exported to XML string attributes (enforced by the export functions).

functions.name: hwloc_export_obj_userdata
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_export_obj_userdata(void *reserved, hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_obj_t obj, const char *name, const void *buffer, size_t length);
functions.description: From within the registered export callback, export object userdata as-is to XML under an optional attribute name. The buffer content of given length is written; only printable characters are allowed in XML attributes. Returns 0 on success, or -1 with errno set to EINVAL if non-printable characters appear in name or buffer.
requirements: Must be called only from inside the export callback set via hwloc_topology_set_userdata_export_callback().
reserved, topology, and obj must be exactly the first three parameters received by the export callback.
name must consist only of printable characters if provided.
buffer content must contain only printable characters; otherwise the call fails with -1 and errno=EINVAL.

Decoding is performed automatically on import before delivering data to the import callback. Returns 0 on success, or -1 with errno set to EINVAL if name contains non-printable characters.
requirements: Must be called only from inside the export callback set via hwloc_topology_set_userdata_export_callback().
reserved, topology, and obj must be exactly the first three parameters received by the export callback.
name must consist only of printable characters; otherwise the call fails with -1 and errno=EINVAL.

functions.name: hwloc_topology_set_userdata_import_callback
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC void hwloc_topology_set_userdata_import_callback(hwloc_topology_t topology, void (*import_cb)(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_obj_t obj, const char *name, const void *buffer, size_t length));

This function should be called before hwloc_topology_load().
import_cb may be NULL to ignore userdata on import.
During invocation, object attributes are readable but links between objects are not yet established.
buffer contains length bytes and is followed by a '\0' byte.

functions.name: hwloc_topology_export_synthetic
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_topology_export_synthetic(hwloc_topology_t topology, char *buffer, size_t buflen, unsigned long flags);
functions.description: Export a topology as a synthetic description string suitable for hwloc_topology_set_synthetic(). Writes at most buflen bytes including the terminating '\0'. Returns the number of characters written (excluding the terminator), or -1 if export fails (e.g., non-symmetric topology). I/O and Misc children are ignored in the export; only normal children are described.
A 1024-byte buffer is generally sufficient for most topologies (advisory).

functions.name: hwloc_backend_alloc
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC struct hwloc_backend * hwloc_backend_alloc(struct hwloc_topology *topology, struct hwloc_disc_component *component, unsigned long private_data_size);
functions.description: Allocate and initialize a discovery backend instance for a topology from a discovery component. Sets default fields; if private_data_size > 0, allocates extra storage after the struct accessible via HWLOC_BACKEND_PRIVATE_DATA(). Caller typically tweaks fields and then calls hwloc_backend_enable() to activate.
requirements: topology must refer to an initialized hwloc_topology
component must point to a valid struct hwloc_disc_component
private_data_size may be 0; if positive, that many bytes of private space is reserved at the end of the backend structure
Caller must call hwloc_backend_enable(backend) to actually enable the backend after any needed customization
Do not access fields assumed core-reserved except via documented mechanisms (e.g., HWLOC_BACKEND_PRIVATE_DATA)

functions.name: hwloc_backend_enable
functions.description: Enable a previously allocated and set up discovery backend so it participates in topology discovery.
requirements: backend must have been returned by hwloc_backend_alloc() for the same topology
backend must be properly initialized by the component as needed before enabling

functions.name: hwloc_plugin_check_namespace
functions.signature: static __hwloc_inline int hwloc_plugin_check_namespace(const char *pluginname, const char *symbol);
functions.description: Sanity-check (from within a plugin) that libhwloc core symbols are visible for dynamic lookup, avoiding lazy-resolution failures. Intended to be called from a plugin’s init() callback. Returns 0 on success, -1 if the specified core symbol cannot be found in the process namespace (in which case the plugin should disable itself). When not built as a plugin (HWLOC_INSIDE_PLUGIN not defined), this function is a no-op returning 0.
requirements: Should be called by plugins in their component init() callback
pluginname should be a non-NULL string identifying the plugin (used for diagnostics)
symbol should name a libhwloc core symbol expected to be resolvable
Build system must define HWLOC_INSIDE_PLUGIN when building the caller as a plugin for the checks to run

functions.name: hwloc_show_errors_mask
functions.description: Get the current mask of error/reporting messages to display, as an OR’ed set of HWLOC_SHOWMSG_* flags. Used with HWLOC_SHOW_ERRORS(flag) to test categories enabled by env (e.g., HWLOC_SHOW_ERRORS).

functions.name: hwloc__insert_object_by_cpuset
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC hwloc_obj_t hwloc__insert_object_by_cpuset(struct hwloc_topology *topology, hwloc_obj_t root, hwloc_obj_t obj, const char *reason);
functions.description: Insert a new object into the topology tree according to cpuset inclusion, starting under root (or the topology root if root is NULL). If the cpuset is empty, type/attributes must be sufficient to place the object (e.g., NUMA nodes with memory). May merge with an identical existing object. Should be called only before levels are built.
requirements: topology must be a valid hwloc topology under construction
root may be NULL or an existing object within topology
obj must be a newly allocated object with no children
Caller should ensure the object type is not filtered out before calling
If obj->cpuset is empty, the object’s type/attributes must allow unambiguous placement
reason should be a unique string identifying the insertion site for diagnostics
Must be called before levels are built/reconnected

functions.name: hwloc_insert_object_by_parent
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC void hwloc_insert_object_by_parent(struct hwloc_topology *topology, hwloc_obj_t parent, hwloc_obj_t obj);
functions.description: Insert an object as the last child of the specified parent, ignoring cpusets. Intended for I/O or other objects where cpuset placement is not meaningful. When importing/duplicating normal children with cpusets, caller must ensure order and disjointness.
requirements: topology must be a valid hwloc topology under construction
parent must be a valid object already in topology
obj may have normal, I/O or Misc children; these children must already have valid parent and next_sibling pointers and be in order
When used for normal children with cpusets, children must be inserted in order and with non-intersecting cpusets
Caller should ensure the object type is not filtered out before calling

functions.name: hwloc_alloc_setup_object
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC hwloc_obj_t hwloc_alloc_setup_object(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_obj_type_t type, unsigned os_index);
functions.description: Allocate and initialize a new hwloc object of the given type and OS index, ready to be configured and inserted into a topology.
requirements: If the OS index is unknown or irrelevant, pass HWLOC_UNKNOWN_INDEX
topology should be a valid topology handle (used for allocation/initialization context)

functions.name: hwloc_obj_add_children_sets
functions.description: Compute and set an object’s cpuset/nodeset by OR’ing the sets of all its children. Used when inserting a parent late (e.g., hostbridge parent, Group from distances).
requirements: obj must have valid children whose cpusets/nodesets are initialized
Intended for scenarios where a new parent is added after children exist

functions.name: hwloc_topology_reconnect
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_topology_reconnect(hwloc_topology_t topology, unsigned long flags __hwloc_attribute_unused);
functions.description: Request reconnection of children arrays and levels within the topology. Useful during discovery when backends need consistent lists/levels.
requirements: topology must be valid and under construction during discovery
flags must be 0 (currently unused)

functions.name: hwloc_pcidisc_find_cap
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC unsigned hwloc_pcidisc_find_cap(const unsigned char *config, unsigned cap);
functions.description: Scan a PCI 256-byte configuration space buffer to find the offset of a given capability ID (cap). Unknown/unavailable bytes should be set to 0xff.
requirements: config must point to a 256-byte PCI config space buffer
Unknown/unavailable bytes in config should be set to 0xff
cap must be a PCI capability ID value

functions.name: hwloc_pcidisc_find_linkspeed
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_pcidisc_find_linkspeed(const unsigned char *config, unsigned offset, float *linkspeed);
functions.description: Read PCI Express capability registers from config (starting at ‘offset’) to determine the link speed and store it in linkspeed. Requires 20 bytes of the PCIe capability block up to the Link Status register.
requirements: config must contain at least 20 valid bytes of the PCIe capability block starting at offset
offset must be the position of PCI_CAP_ID_EXP within config
linkspeed must be a valid pointer to receive the speed value

functions.name: hwloc_pcidisc_check_bridge_type
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC hwloc_obj_type_t hwloc_pcidisc_check_bridge_type(unsigned device_class, const unsigned char *config);
functions.description: Determine whether a PCI function with the given class and configuration header is a PCI device or a PCI bridge, returning the corresponding hwloc object type. Requires the common header to be present.
requirements: config must provide at least 16 bytes of the common PCI configuration header at the beginning
device_class must be the PCI class code for the device

functions.name: hwloc_pcidisc_find_bridge_buses
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_pcidisc_find_bridge_buses(unsigned domain, unsigned bus, unsigned dev, unsigned func, unsigned *secondary_busp, unsigned *subordinate_busp, const unsigned char *config);
functions.description: Extract the secondary and subordinate bus numbers of a PCI bridge from its configuration space and return them via output parameters. Requires the common header to be present. Note: The comment mentions destroying an object on error, but this function does not take an object parameter; treat that note as a documentation inconsistency.
requirements: config must provide at least 32 bytes of the common PCI configuration header at the beginning
secondary_busp and subordinate_busp must be valid pointers for outputs
domain, bus, dev, func identify the PCI function being parsed

functions.name: hwloc_pcidisc_tree_insert_by_busid
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC void hwloc_pcidisc_tree_insert_by_busid(struct hwloc_obj **treep, struct hwloc_obj *obj);
functions.description: Insert a PCI object into a PCI tree according to its bus/device/function (and domain) identifiers. If *treep is NULL, the new object becomes the root there.
requirements: treep must be a valid pointer to a struct hwloc_obj* (may initially point to NULL)
obj must be a valid PCI object with its bus ID fields populated

functions.name: hwloc_pcidisc_tree_attach
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_pcidisc_tree_attach(struct hwloc_topology *topology, struct hwloc_obj *tree);
functions.description: Add host bridges on top of a PCI object tree as needed and attach the resulting hierarchy into the topology so that other backends can find PCI objects/localities.
requirements: topology must be a valid topology handle
tree must point to a valid PCI subtree assembled by the PCI discovery helpers

functions.name: hwloc_pci_find_parent_by_busid
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC struct hwloc_obj * hwloc_pci_find_parent_by_busid(struct hwloc_topology *topology, unsigned domain, unsigned bus, unsigned dev, unsigned func);
functions.description: Find the best parent object for attaching an entity whose locality is specified by a PCI bus ID. Returns the exact PCI device if present, otherwise a suitable ancestor (e.g., bridge) or a nearby CPU object such as the local package.
requirements: topology must be valid and already contain PCI objects (as applicable)
domain, bus, dev, func must identify the target PCI function

functions.name: hwloc_pci_find_by_busid
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC struct hwloc_obj * hwloc_pci_find_by_busid(struct hwloc_topology *topology, unsigned domain, unsigned bus, unsigned dev, unsigned func);
functions.description: Locate the PCI device or bridge that exactly matches the specified bus ID in the topology. Useful for attaching information based on exact PCI IDs. For locality-based attachment, prefer hwloc_pci_find_parent_by_busid().
requirements: topology must be valid and contain PCI objects
domain, bus, dev, func must exactly identify the PCI function sought

functions.name: hwloc_backend_distances_add_create
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC hwloc_backend_distances_add_handle_t hwloc_backend_distances_add_create(hwloc_topology_t topology, const char *name, unsigned long kind, unsigned long flags);
functions.description: Create a new empty distances structure (backend variant) to be populated during discovery. Semantically similar to hwloc_distances_add_create() but tailored for backends.
requirements: topology must be a valid topology under discovery
name, kind, flags as per distances semantics (flags are backend variant parameters)

functions.name: hwloc_backend_distances_add_values
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_backend_distances_add_values(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_backend_distances_add_handle_t handle, unsigned nbobjs, hwloc_obj_t *objs, hwloc_uint64_t *values, unsigned long flags);
functions.description: Specify objects and their pairwise distance values for a backend-created distances structure. Unlike the generic API, objs and values are not duplicated; on success they are attached to the topology and must not be freed by the caller.
requirements: topology must be valid
handle must be obtained from hwloc_backend_distances_add_create() and still open
nbobjs must match the dimensions implied by values (nbobjs x nbobjs)
objs must point to an array of nbobjs valid objects
values must point to an array of nbobjs*nbobjs distance values
On success, the caller must not free objs or values arrays anymore
flags are backend-variant parameters

functions.name: hwloc_backend_distances_add_commit
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_backend_distances_add_commit(hwloc_topology_t topology, hwloc_backend_distances_add_handle_t handle, unsigned long flags);
functions.description: Commit a backend-created distances structure previously created and populated, finalizing its addition to the topology. Backend-oriented variant of hwloc_distances_add_commit().
requirements: topology must be valid
handle must refer to a distances structure created by hwloc_backend_distances_add_create() and populated as required
flags are backend-variant parameters

functions.name: hwloc_linux_set_tid_cpubind
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_linux_set_tid_cpubind(hwloc_topology_t topology, pid_t tid, hwloc_const_cpuset_t set);
functions.description: Bind a Linux thread (TID) to the CPUs specified by the given hwloc cpuset. Behavior matches Linux sched_setaffinity but takes an hwloc cpuset and a topology handle. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error. Use when you need to constrain a specific thread to run only on given processing units. Equivalent to calling hwloc_set_proc_cpubind() with HWLOC_CPUBIND_THREAD.
requirements: topology must be a valid, initialized, and loaded hwloc topology object (via hwloc_topology_init/hwloc_topology_load).
tid must be a valid Linux thread ID (TID) for a thread on the local system.
Caller must have permission to change the affinity of the target thread (same user or appropriate capabilities as required by sched_setaffinity).
set must be a valid, initialized hwloc cpuset; CPUs outside the system topology are ignored or cause failure per OS policy.
Caller must check the return value (0 success, -1 error) and handle errors accordingly.

functions.name: hwloc_linux_get_tid_cpubind
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_linux_get_tid_cpubind(hwloc_topology_t topology, pid_t tid, hwloc_cpuset_t set);
functions.description: Retrieve the current CPU binding of a Linux thread (TID) into an hwloc cpuset previously allocated by the caller. Behavior matches Linux sched_getaffinity but fills an hwloc cpuset. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error. Use to query which PUs a thread is allowed to run on. Equivalent to hwloc_get_proc_cpubind() with HWLOC_CPUBIND_THREAD.
requirements: topology must be a valid, initialized, and loaded hwloc topology object.
tid must be a valid Linux thread ID for a thread on the local system.
set must be a valid, allocated hwloc cpuset; its contents will be overwritten.
Caller must check the return value (0 success, -1 error) and handle errors accordingly.

functions.name: hwloc_linux_get_tid_last_cpu_location
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_linux_get_tid_last_cpu_location(hwloc_topology_t topology, pid_t tid, hwloc_bitmap_t set);
functions.description: Get the last physical CPU (PU) where the specified Linux thread (TID) ran, storing the result into an hwloc bitmap provided by the caller. On success the bitmap contains exactly the PU of the last execution location. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error. Equivalent to hwloc_get_proc_last_cpu_location() with HWLOC_CPUBIND_THREAD.
requirements: topology must be a valid, initialized, and loaded hwloc topology object.
tid must be a valid Linux thread ID for a thread on the local system.
set must be a valid, allocated hwloc bitmap; its contents will be overwritten.
Caller must check the return value (0 success, -1 error) and handle errors accordingly.

functions.name: hwloc_linux_read_path_as_cpumask
functions.signature: HWLOC_DECLSPEC int hwloc_linux_read_path_as_cpumask(const char *path, hwloc_bitmap_t set);
functions.description: Parse a Linux kernel cpumask file at the given path and convert it into an hwloc bitmap. Useful for reading sysfs attributes (e.g., CPU topology, cache cpumaps, or device local_cpus). Returns 0 on success, -1 on error. Note: this function ignores the HWLOC_FSROOT environment variable.
requirements: path must reference a readable file containing a Linux kernel cpumask in the expected textual format (e.g., hex list as used in sysfs).
set must be a valid, allocated hwloc bitmap; its contents will be overwritten.
Because HWLOC_FSROOT is ignored, path must be valid in the host filesystem namespace.
Caller must check the return value (0 success, -1 error) and handle errors accordingly.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets a "generic string" data type consumed by many hwloc stubs
# via FUZZ_PARAM_STR and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME. We aim to produce valid and
# interesting strings that exercise different code paths while remaining plausible
# inputs for names, keys, values, separators, subtype strings, component names,
# PCI busid strings, bitmap strings, XML paths, etc.
#
# The buffer format:
#  - It is a concatenation of multiple null-terminated strings (C-strings), so
#    the fuzzer can split/reuse them for successive FUZZ_PARAM_STR() requests.
#  - We include a mix of: common hwloc memattr names, typical info keys/values,
#    separators, valid PCI busid strings, bitmap formats (hex/list/taskset),
#    XML-like names, component names, and a valid filename.
#  - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.
#
# Consumers:
#  - hwloc_memattr_* APIs: need recognizable attribute names; include predefined
#    ones such as "Capacity", "Bandwidth", "ReadBandwidth", "WriteBandwidth",
#    "Latency", "ReadLatency", "WriteLatency", and also custom names.
#  - hwloc_get_pcidev_by_busidstring: include valid short/long PCI busid strings.
#  - hwloc_bitmap_*_sscanf: include valid hex, list, taskset-style bitmaps.
#  - hwloc_topology_diff_export_xml / _xmlbuffer: include a plausible filename.
#  - obj/info APIs: include non-empty names and varied separators.
#
# The generate() function returns bytes with embedded NULs as separators.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096


def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, seq: List[str]) -> str:
    return seq[rng.randrange(len(seq))]


def _rand_ident(rng: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=24) -> str:
    # Alnum plus _-.: allows keys, names, prefixes, file-ish components
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-.:"
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return "".join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))


def _rand_utf8(rng: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=64) -> str:
    # Mix ASCII with some safe UTF-8 ranges
    parts = []
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    for _ in range(n):
        t = rng.random()
        if t < 0.8:
            parts.append(rng.choice(string.printable[:-5]))  # avoid whitespace extremes mostly
        elif t < 0.9:
            cp = rng.randint(0x00A1, 0x024F)  # Latin-1 supplement/extended
            parts.append(chr(cp))
        else:
            cp = rng.randint(0x0370, 0x03FF)  # Greek
            parts.append(chr(cp))
    s = "".join(parts)
    # Avoid embedded NULs in strings themselves; we will use NUL as separator.
    return s.replace("\x00", " ")


def _valid_pci_busid(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    domain = rng.randrange(0, 0x10000)
    bus = rng.randrange(0, 256)
    dev = rng.randrange(0, 32)
    func = rng.randrange(0, 8)
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        return f"{bus:02x}:{dev:02x}.{func:x}"
    else:
        return f"{domain:04x}:{bus:02x}:{dev:02x}.{func:x}"


def _bitmap_hex_blocks(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # hwloc_bitmap_sscanf expects hex blocks separated by ',' optionally with indexes '@'
    # Provide simple valid cases
    blocks = []
    k = rng.randint(1, 4)
    for _ in range(k):
        # generate 1-4 hex bytes
        nibbles = rng.randint(1, 8)
        h = ''.join(rng.choice('0123456789abcdef') for _ in range(nibbles))
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            # include an index with @
            idx = rng.randint(0, 8)
            blocks.append(f"{h}@{idx}")
        else:
            blocks.append(h)
    return ",".join(blocks)


def _bitmap_list(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # e.g., "0-3,8,10-12"
    parts = []
    base = 0
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 5)):
        start = base + rng.randint(0, 4)
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            end = start + rng.randint(0, 8)
            if end == start:
                parts.append(str(start))
            else:
                parts.append(f"{start}-{end}")
        else:
            parts.append(str(start))
        base = start
    return ",".join(parts)


def _bitmap_taskset(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Hex mask like taskset, optionally comma-separated for multiple longs
    chunks = rng.randint(1, 3)
    return ",".join(''.join(rng.choice('0123456789abcdef') for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 8))) for _ in range(chunks))


def _valid_filename(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Provide a plausible temp filename path
    prefixes = ["/tmp/", "/var/tmp/", "/dev/shm/", "./", "./out/", "./tmp/"]
    name = _rand_ident(rng, 4, 16)
    ext = _rand_choice(rng, [".xml", ".txt", ".dat", ".bin", ".log"]) if rng.random() < 0.8 else ""
    return _rand_choice(rng, prefixes) + name + ext


def _memattr_names() -> List[str]:
    return [
        "Capacity",
        "Locality",
        "Bandwidth",
        "ReadBandwidth",
        "WriteBandwidth",
        "Latency",
        "ReadLatency",
        "WriteLatency",
    ]


def _separators() -> List[str]:
    return [",", " ", "|", ";", "/", "::", "=", ": ", "\t", "/ "]


def _component_names() -> List[str]:
    return [
        "linux",
        "x86",
        "cuda",
        "opencl",
        "noos",
        "xml",
        "synthetic",
        "pci",
        "hwdata",
    ]


def _infos_keys() -> List[str]:
    return [
        "Model",
        "Vendor",
        "Frequency",
        "CacheSize",
        "OSName",
        "KernelRelease",
        "Serial",
        "SKU",
        "UUID",
    ]


def _build_strings(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    out: List[str] = []

    # Include several memattr names (exact matches help find attributes)
    memattrs = _memattr_names()
    rng.shuffle(memattrs)
    out.extend(memattrs)

    # Also include a few custom attributes that may be registered and used
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5)):
        out.append("custom_" + _rand_ident(rng, 5, 14))

    # Include common separators
    seps = list(_separators())
    rng.shuffle(seps)
    out.extend(seps[:rng.randint(3, len(seps))])

    # Valid PCI busid strings
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5)):
        out.append(_valid_pci_busid(rng))

    # Bitmap strings for three parsers
    out.append(_bitmap_hex_blocks(rng))
    out.append(_bitmap_list(rng))
    out.append(_bitmap_taskset(rng))

    # Infos keys and sample values
    keys = list(_infos_keys())
    rng.shuffle(keys)
    out.extend(keys[:rng.randint(3, len(keys))])
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 8)):
        out.append(_rand_utf8(rng, 3, 24))

    # Component names and a few random identifiers
    comps = list(_component_names())
    rng.shuffle(comps)
    out.extend(comps[:rng.randint(3, len(comps))])
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 6)):
        out.append(_rand_ident(rng, 3, 18))

    # Subtype/name prefixes used in some queries
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 6)):
        out.append(_rand_ident(rng, 2, 10))

    # Filename for XML export or other file-accepting APIs
    out.append(_valid_filename(rng))

    # Add a couple of longer strings as stress but valid text
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        out.append(_rand_utf8(rng, 32, 96))

    # Ensure at least one non-empty simple string for APIs requiring non-empty
    out.append("name")
    out.append("value")

    return out


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    strings = _build_strings(rng)

    # Shuffle to vary early-consumption strings
    rng.shuffle(strings)

    # Encode as null-terminated concatenation
    out_bytes = bytearray()
    for s in strings:
        b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
        if len(b) > 512:
            b = b[:512]
        # Ensure no embedded NULs to keep split semantics predictable
        b = b.replace(b"\x00", b" ")
        if len(out_bytes) + len(b) + 1 > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        out_bytes += b + b"\x00"

    # Guarantee at least one filename and one memattr present; if not, append minimal
    need_append = []
    if not any(x in out_bytes for x in (b"Capacity\x00", b"Latency\x00", b"Bandwidth\x00")):
        need_append.append(_rand_choice(rng, _memattr_names()))
    if b"/tmp/" not in out_bytes and b"./" not in out_bytes:
        need_append.append(_valid_filename(rng))
    for s in need_append:
        b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore').replace(b"\x00", b" ")
        if len(out_bytes) + len(b) + 1 > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        out_bytes += b + b"\x00"

    return bytes(out_bytes)
